items.title: window.document is writable, unlike Chrome's non-configurable getter-only attribute
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability (those go through SECURITY.md, not a public issue).

### obscura version or commit

8b49681 (main)

### OS and architecture

Windows 11 x64

### How are you using obscura?

CLI (fetch / serve / scrape / mcp)

### Affected area

JavaScript or DOM behavior

### Build variant

Render-enabled with stealth (official stealth archive or --features render,stealth)

### Stealth mode

On (--stealth)

### Reproduction

The issue is observable without relying on a specific website.

Run:

```powershell
obscura fetch "data:text/html,<html><body></body></html>" `
  --eval "(() => { const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, 'document'); return JSON.stringify({ hasGet: typeof d.get, hasSet: typeof d.set, writable: d.writable, configurable: d.configurable, enumerable: d.enumerable, constructor: document.constructor.name }); })()"
```

Then run a non-strict assignment:

```powershell
obscura fetch "data:text/html,<html><body></body></html>" `
  --eval "document = { probe: true }; String(document.constructor.name + ':' + typeof document.body + ':' + typeof document.cookie)"
```

Run the same descriptor and assignment checks in Chrome DevTools for comparison.

### Expected behavior

`window.document` should match Chrome's attribute semantics:

- it is exposed as an enumerable, non-configurable accessor;
- the accessor has a getter and no setter;
- assignment in sloppy mode is ignored;
- assignment in strict mode throws `TypeError`.

After either assignment form, `document` should remain the live `Document`, and `document.body`, `document.cookie`, and `document.scripts` should remain usable.

### Actual behavior

On the affected revision, Obscura exposes `document` as a writable and configurable own data property:

```text
hasGet: false
writable: true
configurable: true
enumerable: true
```

Executing `document = { probe: true }` replaces the live `Document` with a plain object. Afterwards, `document.body`, `document.cookie`, and `document.scripts` are all `undefined`.

In Chromium 151 on Windows, the same checks report:

```text
hasGet: true
hasSet: false
configurable: false
enumerable: true
```

The assignment is silently ignored in sloppy mode, and `document` remains an `HTMLDocument` with working `body`, `cookie`, and `scripts` properties.

This was encountered while a page challenge VM used a dynamically generated `eval` to assign `document = {}`. The replacement caused subsequent page code that needed `document.cookie` to fail. The issue here is the generic Window attribute semantics, not a request to implement challenge-specific behavior.

Related: #1141 tracks broader DOM conformance gaps.

### Rendering details

Not applicable

### Does headless Chrome behave the same?

No: headless Chrome renders or behaves correctly and obscura does not

### Logs

```shell
Observed on `8b49681` with the render and stealth configuration. No exception is raised in sloppy mode; the write silently succeeds and replaces the live document.

Obscura before assignment:

document.constructor.name = Document
typeof document.body     = object
typeof document.cookie   = string
typeof document.scripts  = object


Obscura after `document = { probe: true }`:

document.constructor.name = Object
typeof document.body     = undefined
typeof document.cookie   = undefined
typeof document.scripts  = undefined


A focused regression should assert both the descriptor shape and the non-strict/strict assignment behavior. No network access is required for this reproduction.
```

items.title: fetch() and XMLHttpRequest send no Sec-Fetch-* headers
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability.

### obscura version or commit

v0.2.5, official `obscura-aarch64-macos` archive (render build)

### OS and architecture

macOS 26, arm64

### How are you using obscura?

`obscura serve` driven by Playwright over CDP

### Affected area

Networking: request headers for script-initiated requests

### Build variant

Render

### Reproduction

A server that echoes `Sec-Fetch-*` and `Referer` request headers, and a same-origin page that calls it:

```js
await fetch('/echo').then(r => r.json())
// XMLHttpRequest to the same URL gives the same result
```

- Chrome 151: `{"Sec-Fetch-Site":"same-origin","Sec-Fetch-Mode":"cors","Sec-Fetch-Dest":"empty","Referer":"http://127.0.0.1:…/"}`
- Obscura: `{}`, for both `fetch()` and `XMLHttpRequest`

### Expected

The Fetch Metadata headers (`Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Sec-Fetch-Mode`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest`) on script requests, which all current major browsers send.

Servers use `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` to accept requests from their own pages without a token (a common CSRF guard and local-app auth pattern). Without it, those API calls return 401 under Obscura and the page renders error states that never happen in a browser, which an automation agent then reports as application bugs. Found this way on a FastAPI app whose same-origin API guard checks exactly this header.

The missing `Referer` on the same requests is already tracked in #875.

items.title: CDP DOM domain: requestNode, getNodeForLocation, requestChildNodes and getAttributes are unimplemented (breaks go-rod, ferrum, chromedp)
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability.

### obscura version or commit

v0.2.5, official `obscura-aarch64-macos` archive (render build)

### OS and architecture

macOS 26, arm64

### How are you using obscura?

`obscura serve` driven over CDP (go-rod, ferrum, chromedp; reproduced below with a raw CDP session)

### Affected area

CDP: DOM domain

### Build variant

Render

### Reproduction

Against `obscura serve`, on a page containing `<label id=lab for=c>agree</label>`:

| CDP call | Chrome 151 | Obscura |
|---|---|---|
| `DOM.getNodeForLocation {x, y}` (point inside the label) | `{nodeId, backendNodeId, frameId}` | `-32601 Unknown DOM method: getNodeForLocation` |
| `DOM.requestNode {objectId}` (objectId from `Runtime.evaluate`) | `{nodeId}` | `Unknown DOM method: requestNode` |
| `DOM.requestChildNodes {nodeId: <html>, depth: 1}` | `DOM.setChildNodes` event with 2 nodes | `Unknown DOM method: requestChildNodes` |
| `DOM.getAttributes {nodeId}` | `["id","lab","for","c"]` | `Unknown DOM method: getAttributes` |
| `DOM.getDocument {depth:-1}`, then append a node from JS | `DOM.childNodeInserted` event | no event |

### Expected

These are the node-tracking calls the non-Node CDP clients build on, and each one breaks a basic flow:

- **go-rod**: `element.Click()` calls `DOM.getNodeForLocation` to confirm the hit target, so every click fails with the error above.
- **ferrum**: `fill`/`click` resolve nodes through `DOM.requestNode` and fail immediately.
- **chromedp**: selector queries load the node tree through `DOM.requestChildNodes` and the `DOM.setChildNodes`/`childNodeInserted` events, so `SendKeys`/`Click` time out waiting for the node.

In the Lexbench headless-browser benchmark (lexmount/Lexbench-Headless-Browser) these drivers fail the same simple login → add-to-cart flows that pass under Puppeteer and Playwright: on this v0.2.5 render build chromedp passes 38/92, ferrum 42/92, rod 63/92, versus Playwright 119/142 and Puppeteer 106/143.

items.title: WebCrypto public-key algorithms (RSA-OAEP, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, RSA-PSS, ECDSA, ECDH, Ed25519): which backend?
items.body:
### Area

JavaScript or DOM behavior

### Problem

`crypto.subtle` covers the secret-key algorithms (HMAC, AES-GCM/CBC/CTR, PBKDF2, HKDF), and the shim notes that the public-key ones throw `NotSupportedError` for now. Real pages hit them during login and API flows:

- bank and payment logins that encrypt the password with the server's RSA-OAEP public key before posting it;
- OIDC / JWT libraries verifying RS256, PS256 or ES256 tokens in the page;
- ECDH / X25519 for end-to-end encrypted apps.

On those pages automation stops at the login form.

### Proposed solution

I'd like to contribute these, one algorithm per PR, starting with RSA-OAEP (generateKey, importKey / exportKey for spki, pkcs8 and jwk, encrypt / decrypt), then RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, RSA-PSS, ECDSA, ECDH and Ed25519/X25519. Each would come with `obscura-js` tests and before/after WPT numbers for the WebCryptoAPI files it touches.

Before writing code, the crypto backend is your call, and that's what I'd like to agree on here:

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| RustCrypto `rsa` (+ `p256` / `p384` / `ecdsa`, `ed25519-dalek`, `x25519-dalek`) | Pure Rust, same family as the current `aes` / `hmac` / `pbkdf2` / `hkdf` | `rsa` has RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin timing side channel, no fixed release), which the `deny.toml` advisories check would fail on |
| `ring` (already in the tree through rustls) | No new dependency, widely audited; RSA PKCS#1 / PSS and ECDSA P-256 / P-384 sign and verify, Ed25519 | No RSA key generation and no RSA-OAEP; ECDH / X25519 only with ephemeral keys, so no imported ECDH keys |
| `aws-lc-rs` | Covers everything (OAEP, key generation, all curves) | Brings a C build (CMake), which the render build avoids today |

Which would you prefer?

### Alternatives considered

If none of these fits, I can start with what `ring` covers (signature verification and signing with imported keys) and leave RSA-OAEP and key generation for later.

### Scope

- [x] This should not regress performance (obscura's speed and memory footprint are a hard constraint).
- [ ] I described the expected visual output if this affects rendering.
- [x] This is not detection-evasion for abusive purposes.

items.title: 0.2.5: "ReferenceError: cdApi is not defined" logged 14x during login submit — uppopi SDK still never inserted
items.body:
### Summary

On **obscura 0.2.5** (official `obscura-aarch64-linux-stealth` binary, driven **without** `--stealth`), a real bank login flow at Banco Galicia now logs this **14× per run**:

```
ERROR obscura::console: Error while trying to set CSID and/or Context: ReferenceError: cdApi is not defined
```

It appears **right after the login form is submitted**, before the bank confirms the session. This is a follow-up to #851 (closed as fixed in 0.2.4): in 0.2.5 the old `There is no supported http request object` errors dropped from **16 to 3**, but the anti-fraud SDK still never injects `uppopi-*-sb.min.js`, and the missing global now surfaces as `cdApi is not defined`.

The bank **still accepts the login** on 0.2.5 (login OK, movements fetched, the 4 ARS transactions are the same ones the previous 0.2.4 run had already imported — worker deduplicated 4/4), so this is not an auth blocker — it is an anti-fraud SDK fidelity issue.

### Environment

- obscura **0.2.5**, asset `obscura-aarch64-linux-stealth.tar.gz`, sha256 `e28ed5ff2dbabe8d820c7b1ef56e6005399aff15912c7774777719e66a021a32`
- Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB), Debian 12 bookworm, aarch64, Node v22.23.1, puppeteer-core 23.11.1
- `obscura serve --port 9222` — **no `--stealth`**
- Env: `OBSCURA_BLOCK_TRACKERS=0`, `OBSCURA_TIMEZONE=America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires`, `OBSCURA_GEOLOCATION=-34.6037,-58.3816`, `OBSCURA_NAV_TIMEOUT_MS=120000`, `OBSCURA_SCRIPT_DEADLINE_MS=90000`, `OBSCURA_MODULE_BUDGET_MS=15000`, `OBSCURA_CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=180000`
- Site: `https://onlinebanking.bancogalicia.com.ar/login` (BGSensors / "cd" SDK, loaded dynamically from `portals3.galicia.ar`)

### Measured A/B

Same site, same account, one production run per hour. Counts are per run, parsed from the engine stderr:

| run (local) | obscura | `cdApi is not defined` | `no supported http request object` | `V8 watchdog` | `decoding response body` | login |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2026-10-17 15:00 | 0.2.4 | 1 | 24 | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| 2026-10-17 16:00 | 0.2.4 | 0 | 23 | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| 2026-10-17 17:00 | 0.2.4 | 0 | 23 | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| 2026-10-17 18:00 | 0.2.4 | 0 | 24 | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| 2026-10-17 19:00 | 0.2.4 | 0 | 24 | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| **2026-10-17 20:00** | **0.2.5** | **14** | **5** | 0 | 0 | ✅ |

The message existed at low frequency on 0.2.4 (1 occurrence in one run), so it is not strictly new — but 0.2.5 makes it fire 14× per run. All other engine messages are unchanged (`KeepAlive` JSONP `Unexpected token '<'`, `Dynamic script fetch error: HTTP 404`, `verResumen` / `banner_galicia_mas_btn` missing, `CRED_PREFIXES` re-declaration, CDP `callFunctionOn` context/timeout warnings).

### Log excerpt (0.2.5, first occurrence)

```
Enviando formulario...
[obscura] WARN  obscura_browser::page: Script error (…/bundles/sharedin?…): JS error: Uncaught SyntaxError: Identifier 'CRED_PREFIXES' has already been declared
[obscura] ERROR obscura::console: El elemento con id "verResumen" no se encontró en el DOM.
[obscura] ERROR obscura::console: Dynamic script fetch error: HTTP 404
[obscura] ERROR obscura::console: Error while trying to set CSID and/or Context: ReferenceError: cdApi is not defined
[obscura] ERROR obscura::console: Worker error: There is no supported http request object
Esperando respuesta del servidor...
Login exitoso
[obscura] ERROR obscura::console: Interval error: Error: There is no supported http request object
```

The 14 occurrences span the whole session (23:01:35 → 23:03:56 UTC), roughly one every few seconds during login and the subsequent movements/receipts flow.

### What I checked (risk-0, no credentials submitted)

- Loading the login page and waiting **60 s without submitting** does **not** reproduce it in either 0.2.5 or 0.2.4 (CDP console hook). The trigger is the submit/response cycle.
- `portals3.galicia.ar/cdn/ca/hero-app.js` (5.3 KB loader) dynamically inserts `portals3.galicia.ar/cdn/ca/jquery-3.6.1.min.js` (a ~2.9 MB obfuscated bundle). **Neither file contains `cdApi`, `set CSID`, or `CSID`**, so `cdApi` is expected from a later script in the chain.
- `verify-uppopi.js` (loads the login page, no credentials) still reports on 0.2.5: `hasCdSNum: false`, `uppopiRequested: false`, 288 requests. In Chromium the `uppopi-*-sb.min.js` request happens and `cdSNum` is set.
- Hypothesis: `cdApi` is a global defined by the `uppopi` SDK. 0.2.5 fixed the worker HTTP-object failures enough (16 → 3) that the "set CSID and/or Context" code now runs repeatedly; because the SDK still is not inserted, it throws `cdApi is not defined` each time. So this may be the same remaining gap as #851/#518, now with a different symptom rather than a separate engine bug.

### Impact

No auth regression: the bank accepts the login, movements are fetched, and the bank data matches the previous run exactly. The remaining issue is that the anti-fraud SDK still cannot set CSID/context, i.e. the session looks less "verified" than in Chromium.

### Related

- #851 (closed; 0.2.4 fixed the worker/interval errors and the login went through)
- #518, #699, #592, #520 (previous SDK-loading gaps)

items.title: Top-level --user-agent is accepted but ignored (and scrape has no way to set a UA)
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability (those go through SECURITY.md, not a public issue).

### obscura version or commit

0.2.4 (official linux x86_64 release, render build); source checked at main bd95294

### OS and architecture

Linux x86_64 (Debian trixie container under gVisor; Ubuntu 24.04 host)

### How are you using obscura?

CLI (fetch / serve / scrape / mcp)

### Affected area

CLI or MCP

### Build variant

Render-enabled (official default archive or --features render)

### Stealth mode

Off

### Reproduction

```sh
# a loopback server that echoes the User-Agent header it receives
python3 -c 'import http.server as h
class H(h.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(s):
        b=s.headers.get("User-Agent","").encode(); s.send_response(200); s.send_header("Content-Length",str(len(b))); s.end_headers(); s.wfile.write(b)
h.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1",8099),H).serve_forever()' &

U=http://127.0.0.1:8099/
obscura --allow-private-network --user-agent "TestUA/1.0" fetch $U --dump text                 # A: before the subcommand
obscura --allow-private-network fetch --user-agent "TestUA/1.0" $U --dump text                 # B: after the subcommand
obscura --allow-private-network --user-agent "TestUA/1.0" fetch $U --eval navigator.userAgent  # C: what the page sees
```

### Expected behavior

`obscura --help` lists `--user-agent <USER_AGENT>` as a top-level option, so A and C should send and report `TestUA/1.0`, the same as B. Or, if the flag is meant to be subcommand-only, it should be rejected at the top level rather than silently accepted. By contrast, `--stealth`, `--proxy` and `--obey-robots` are declared `global = true`.

### Actual behavior

A and C silently use the built-in default UA. Only B works:

```
A: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/143.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
B: TestUA/1.0
C: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/143.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
```

From the source (`crates/obscura-cli/src/main.rs`, v0.2.4 and `main` at bd95294): `Args::user_agent` is declared `#[arg(long)]`, not `global = true`, and no match arm ever reads `args.user_agent`. Each subcommand arm uses its own `user_agent` field instead. There is no error or warning, so a caller who sets an identifying UA ends up sending the default one without knowing it.

`scrape` has no `--user-agent` of its own, so the top-level flag is the only way to try to set one there, and it is dropped.

`--storage-dir` had the same shape in v0.2.4. `main` now reads `args.storage_dir` for `mcp`; we haven't checked the other subcommands.

Suggested fix: make `user_agent` `global = true` and merge it the way `merge_proxy` does (subcommand value wins), and add `--user-agent` to `scrape`.

Context: we run obscura for sandboxed agents and want them to send an honest, identifying User-Agent. We're working around this by passing the flag after the subcommand.

### Rendering details

_No response_

### Does headless Chrome behave the same?

I did not check

### Logs

```shell

items.title: Worker global scope doesn't expose built-ins on self
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability (those go through SECURITY.md, not a public issue).

### obscura version or commit

v0.2.4

### OS and architecture

Windows 11 Pro x64 (build 26200)

### How are you using obscura?

Other (CDP server via Rod)

### Affected area

JavaScript or DOM behavior

### Build variant

Render-enabled with stealth (official stealth archive or --features render,stealth)

### Stealth mode

Same result with it on and off

### Reproduction

Run this on https://example.com with `Runtime.evaluate` and `awaitPromise: true`:

```js
new Promise((resolve) => {
  const src = "postMessage([typeof Object, typeof self.Object, 'Object' in self, typeof self.Uint8Array])";
  const worker = new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src], { type: "text/javascript" })));
  worker.onmessage = (e) => resolve(e.data);
  worker.onerror = (e) => resolve("error: " + e.message);
  setTimeout(() => resolve("timeout"), 3000);
})
```

### Expected behavior

`["function","function",true,"function"]`, which is what headless Chrome returns.

### Actual behavior

`["function","undefined",false,"undefined"]`. Bare `Object` works, but built-ins aren't reachable through `self`.

A real site's blob worker fails with `Worker error: Object is not defined.` and I think it's the same problem, since obfuscated worker code often looks globals up through `self`.

### Does headless Chrome behave the same?

No: headless Chrome renders or behaves correctly and obscura does not

items.title: Module scripts log 0 bytes and intermittently fail to execute, stranding SPAs on their boot splash
items.body:
## Summary

`<script type="module">` loads are unreliable in two ways, and both break any Vite/webpack SPA:

1. They are logged as **0 bytes** in the network log even though the server sends a normal gzip body. Classic `<script src>` on the same page logs its correct decompressed size.
2. Module execution is **intermittent**. On some loads the module never runs and the page stays on its boot splash. On other loads a later `import()` of a lazy chunk fails with `error sending request`, which throws into the page and lands the app in its error boundary.

## Steps to reproduce

Serve one HTML document that mixes classic and module scripts, all `Content-Encoding: gzip` from the same origin:

```html
<script src="/auth-bridge.js"></script>              <!-- classic -->
<script type="module" src="/assets/index-abc.js"></script>
```

1. `browser_navigate` (MCP) or `Page.navigate` (CDP) to that page.
2. Read `browser_network_requests` (MCP) or the `Network.*` log.

## Actual

```
[200] GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/auth-bridge.js?v=5 (7497B)      <- classic, correct
[200] GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/boot-recovery.js     (5385B)      <- classic, correct
[200] GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/pwa-local.js        (8878B)      <- classic, correct
[200] GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/restore-and-launch.js (0B)       <- module
[200] GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/sync/local-data-adapter.js (0B)  <- module
[200] GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/sync/backup-normalizer.js (0B)   <- module
[200] GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/assets/index-D1Y5F8Lk.js (0B)    <- module entry
```

Every 0 B entry is a module script, every classic script has the right size. `curl -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip'` on the same URLs returns 3375, 3327, 3539 and 8701 compressed bytes respectively, so the bodies are on the wire.

In-page control on the same load:

```
typeof window.isoLogin === "function"          // classic script ran
document.querySelectorAll('#root *').length    // 0, module entry never ran
```

Re-running `import('/assets/index-D1Y5F8Lk.js')` by hand mounts the app immediately.

The second failure shows up later, once the app is running:

```
[error] TypeError: Failed to fetch module http://127.0.0.1:3000/assets/useNotificationStore-BTREori0.js:
        Network error: ... error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:3000/assets/useNotificationStore-BTREori0.js)
```

## Expected

Module scripts report the same body size as classic scripts, execute on load like classic scripts, and `import()` of a same-origin chunk resolves on the first attempt.

## Impact

- Any Vite/webpack SPA can hang on its splash with an empty `#root` and no console error.
- A failed lazy chunk throws into the page. In the app I hit this with, the error boundary rendered and the app tore down its own localStorage session, so every protected route fell back to the signed-out view.
- It is not observable from a plain HTML smoke test, which is why the 0 B accounting in particular has gone unnoticed.

## Environment

- obscura 0.2.3, `obscura mcp` and `obscura serve`, aarch64-linux-android build
- Local server on `127.0.0.1:3000` with `--allow-private-network`
- App under test: Vite SPA, entry `/assets/index-D1Y5F8Lk.js`, 4 module scripts in `index.html`

## Notes

Reporting this separately from #678 (Web Storage does not survive a navigation) because the two are independent. Even with the session kept alive in-process, the module failures above still empty every data store in a local-first app.

items.body:
### Area
JavaScript or DOM behavior

### Problem
For AI agents and automated workflows, session preservation across process restarts and navigations is critical.
While Obscura currently supports `cookies.json` persistence via `--storage-dir`, `localStorage` and `IndexedDB` remain ephemeral in-memory objects in `bootstrap.js` (lines 14390–14500), and `CacheStorage` is currently unadvertised.

Many modern web applications, SPAs, and session managers rely on persistent `localStorage` and `IndexedDB` to maintain auth tokens, refreshed sessions, and offline caches. When restarting or running multiple agent tasks with `--storage-dir`, those sessions are lost.

### Proposed solution
We propose implementing persistent storage under `--storage-dir` in three phased steps:

1. **Persistent `localStorage` Disk Sync:**
   - On page navigation / graceful shutdown, flush origin-scoped storage to `<storage-dir>/localStorage/<sanitized_origin>.json` (matching the documented contract in `docs/Persist-cookies-and-storage.md`).
   - Wire `localStorage` getter/setter in `bootstrap.js` through `deno_core` ops into the origin store.

2. **ACID IndexedDB Engine backed by pure-Rust `redb`:**
   - Avoid C SQLite dependencies to preserve cross-compilation across macOS, Linux, and Windows.
   - Use `redb` (pure-Rust, embedded transactional B-tree store).
   - Store databases at `<storage-dir>/indexeddb/<sanitized_origin>/<db_name>.redb`.
   - Wire `_idbObjectStore`, basic key ranges, and cursor operations (`openCursor`, `openKeyCursor`) through `deno_core` ops.

3. **CacheStorage (`caches`):**
   - Store request/response headers in JSON metadata and body streams under `<storage-dir>/cache_storage/<origin>/<cache_name>/`, allowing `caches.open()`, `cache.match()`, and `cache.put()` to retain real responses.

We have a working development branch and are preparing a PR for Step 1 (`localStorage` disk sync) and Step 2 (`redb` IndexedDB).

### Alternatives considered
- **SQLite / rusqlite:** Requires C compilers / toolchains and complicates cross-compilation across platforms (distroless, Windows MSVC, musl, etc.). Pure-Rust `redb` keeps Obscura's single-binary zero-external-dependency promise.
- **In-memory polyfill alone:** Insufficient for agent session reuse across CLI/CDP runs.

### Scope
- [x] This should not regress performance (obscura's speed and memory footprint are a hard constraint).
- [ ] I described the expected visual output if this affects rendering.
- [x] This is not detection-evasion for abusive purposes.

DOM mutation, MutationObserver, Range and node documents differ from the DOM spec
items.body:
DOM mutation, MutationObserver, Range, node document and some CSSOM behavior differs from the DOM and CSSOM specs and from Chromium. A 22-file WPT subset passes 69 of 169 subtests on `main` (Chromium: 165), and one harness never completes.

**Environment:** `2f6e09a`, release `--features render,stealth`, WPT `8b6e09b0fe80243092050c92ff430a47c2d30b77`, x86_64 Linux.

Main causes, by area:

- **Insertion and removal.**
  - `insertBefore(null, null)` returns silently.
  - Non-Node arguments to `removeChild` throw `NotFoundError` instead of `TypeError`.
  - Document child constraints (one element, one doctype, doctype before element, no text) are not enforced.
  - The order of the pre-insertion checks differs from the spec, so the wrong exception is thrown.
- **MutationObserver records.**
  - Records have no `previousSibling`, `nextSibling` or `attributeNamespace`.
  - Inserting a DocumentFragment produces one record per child.
  - Moving a node produces no removal record on its old parent.
  - `removeAttribute` produces no record.
  - Options are not validated.
- **Range.** `deleteContents`, `extractContents`, `cloneContents` and `surroundContents` are no-ops. Observers waiting on their records never fire, which is the cause of the `MutationObserver-childList.html` timeout.
- **Node documents.** `Node.ownerDocument` always returns the main document. `createHTMLDocument` and `createDocument` return plain objects rather than `Document` nodes.
- **CSSOM.** `@media` rules are opaque `CSSRule` objects, so `mediaRule.insertRule` is not a function. CSSOM rule changes do not invalidate cached computed style.
- **getComputedStyle.** It returns real values for detached elements; Chromium returns an empty declaration.
- **IntersectionObserver.**
  - The callback's `this` is not the observer.
  - Entries are plain objects.
  - `isIntersecting` ignores thresholds.
  - `boundingClientRect.left` is 15 or 19 instead of 11 in two tests. The cause is in layout: inside an `inline-block`, block children share a flex row (auto widths collapse to 0), and formatting whitespace around them takes space.

Minimal checks:

```js
document.body.insertBefore(null, null);            // returns; Chromium throws TypeError
document.implementation.createHTMLDocument("t")
  .createElement("p").ownerDocument === document;  // true; should be the new document
document.createRange().deleteContents;             // runs, removes nothing
getComputedStyle(document.createElement("div")).display;  // "block"; Chromium ""
```

A pull request with the fixes and tests follows.

items.title: Native form POST navigations: missing response after redirect and events sent to an observer session
items.body:
Native form POST navigations are reported incorrectly over CDP. The POST is sent once and the result page loads, but clients do not always receive the navigation response.

**Environment:** `adb4c1a` (unchanged in `a005d16`), release `render,stealth` build, Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64, Playwright over CDP, loopback fixtures.

### 1. POST answered with a redirect has no navigation response

Submit a form with `method="post"`; the server answers `303 See Other` to a result page. Playwright's navigation `Response` is `None` in Obscura and `200` in Chrome. The final page loads correctly.

The navigation's Document network event records the requested URL and a fixed `GET` method. After a redirect the page URL is the final URL, so CDP finds no document event for the navigation. A POST without a redirect is also reported as `GET`.

### 2. An additional CDP session can take the navigation events

With a second CDP session attached to the page (for example `context.new_cdp_session(page)` with `Network.enable`), a native form POST reported its navigation response in 6 of 10 runs; Chrome and Obscura without the extra session: 10 of 10. In every run the server received exactly one correct POST and the result document loaded.

Page-initiated navigations are sent to the first session found in an unordered map, so the observer session can receive the navigation events instead of the page client.

items.title: getBoundingClientRect() returns a fixed placeholder box for every element except <html>/<body>
items.body:
## Description

`getBoundingClientRect()` only computes real layout geometry for the root `<html>` and `<body>` elements. Every other element tested (multiple different elements, across multiple different pages) returned a fixed placeholder box — only the x/y position varied between elements, while width/height stayed constant regardless of the element's actual rendered size.

## Impact

This is a significant correctness gap: `getBoundingClientRect()` is the primary API for reading real layout geometry from JS, and it's relied on by a huge share of visual-regression tooling, scroll/viewport logic, intersection-based animation triggers, and general DOM assertions in tests. With non-root elements returning placeholder dimensions instead of their real box, any test or automation relying on element size/position will silently get wrong data rather than an error — meaning results can look superficially valid while being incorrect.

## Suggested next step

Since this affects nearly any layout-dependent test, it's probably worth prioritizing over more specific gaps (like SVG geometry methods or emulation no-ops) — those are narrower use cases, whereas this one undermines confidence in *any* test that reads element geometry.

items.title: CDP Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled is a no-op; Emulation.setEmulatedMedia not implemented
items.body:
## Description

Two CDP emulation methods used for mobile/responsive testing don't actually do anything under Obscura, but neither one surfaces an error — both calls appear to succeed.

## Details (source-verified)

- `Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled`: implemented as a literal no-op in `crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/emulation.rs:126`. The code comment itself admits: "Touch emulation does not affect layout yet."
- `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`: not implemented at all. The CDP call is swallowed by a catch-all no-op handler, so it silently "succeeds" from the client's point of view but has no effect.

## Impact

There is currently no way to make `pointer: coarse` / `hover: none` (or any `prefers-*`/media-feature override sent via `setEmulatedMedia`) evaluate true through the CDP interface. Any Puppeteer/Playwright script that emulates a touch device or overrides media features for responsive/mobile testing will silently get desktop-pointer behavior instead, with no error to indicate the emulation didn't apply — which is worse than an explicit failure, since it looks like a passing test.

## Suggested fix

At minimum, either implement these against Obscura's layout/media-query engine, or have them return an explicit CDP error / unsupported-method response instead of silently no-op'ing, so callers can detect that emulation isn't actually in effect.

items.title: SVGGeometryElement.getTotalLength() not implemented (prototype chain exists, method throws)
items.body:
## Description

`getTotalLength()` on SVG path/line elements throws `TypeError: ... is not a function` at runtime, even though the `SVGGeometryElement`/`SVGPathElement` prototype chain is otherwise implemented correctly (`instanceof` checks pass).

## Repro

Any page that calls `element.getTotalLength()` on a real `<path>` or `<line>` SVG element (e.g. for a stroke-draw / "draw SVG" animation) throws instead of returning the path length.

Console output when hit via GSAP-driven stroke animation:
```
WARN obscura::console: Invalid property strokeDashoffset set to 100
ERROR obscura::console: Timer error: TypeError: l.getTotalLength is not a function
    at buildViz (script.js:2025:21)
    at App.onReveal.vStart (script.js:2211:21)
```
(The "Missing plugin?" wording in the first warning is GSAP's own generic message when a property write silently fails — misleading here, since the real cause is the missing DOM method, not a missing GSAP plugin.)

## Root cause (source-verified)

In `obscura-js/src/runtime.rs` / `bootstrap.js`: the `SVGGeometryElement`/`SVGPathElement` prototype chain is implemented (confirmed via the existing `instanceof` / prototype-chain test), but no geometry-length computation backs `getTotalLength()` — the method is simply missing from the prototype, so calling it throws.

## Impact

Any page using standard SVG stroke-draw animations (a very common pattern, e.g. via GSAP DrawSVGPlugin-style code, or hand-rolled `stroke-dasharray`/`stroke-dashoffset` animation keyed off path length) will throw at runtime under Obscura, even though the same code runs correctly in every real browser.

<script>
window.events = [];
for (const type of ['input', 'change']) {

}
</script>
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chromium | 50 | 80 | 90 | Two per completed update |
| Obscura | 50 | 50 | 50 | None |

items.title: WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 support: missing generateKey blocks Mercari DPoP API requests
items.body:
## Summary

WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 key generation is unsupported in v0.2.3, preventing Mercari's public seller page from preparing its anonymous API requests. The actual application error is `generateKey does not support ECDSA`; no seller/profile/product API request is emitted, and the page eventually shows a load-failure error.

This is a focused follow-up to #343 / merged #344, which intentionally implemented secret-key algorithms and left ECDSA unsupported. The broader deno_crypto proposal #204 was closed without merging. I searched open and closed issues/PRs for ECDSA, WebCrypto, generateKey, P-256, asymmetric, DPoP, and Mercari and did not find a dedicated ECDSA follow-up.

## Before you start

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs (related work linked above).
- [x] Tested the latest release, v0.2.3.
- [x] This is a browser compatibility report, not a security vulnerability.

## Version and environment

- Official release: `obscura 0.2.3`, release commit `1a3169da276d7720732c7b20535474942917fb83`.
- Linux x86_64, official render-enabled binary, stealth off.
- `obscura serve`, driven by a standalone CDP client; fresh isolated anonymous storage, no existing cookies or credentials imported.
- `--font-dir /usr/share/fonts` was used to avoid an unrelated Japanese font issue.
- Binary SHA-256: `ca649bbd80167e457e7ebf615c5155b7d4fd1984c5ad2bd755253ee1a133e34d`.

## Reproduction (actually exercised)

1. Start the release CDP server on a loopback port with isolated storage.
2. Create a page with `Target.createTarget`, attach using `Target.attachToTarget` with `flatten: true`, and include its session ID in subsequent commands.
3. Enable `Page`, `Runtime`, `Network`, and `Log` before navigation.
4. Navigate to `https://jp.mercari.com/user/profile/669097454` without logging in.
5. Drain events for approximately 65 seconds. Inspect object arguments from `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` with `Runtime.callFunctionOn`, rather than relying only on their shallow descriptions.

Actual application error object:

```json
{
  "name": "APIError",
  "message": "INTERNAL ERROR",
  "kind": "INTERNAL ERROR",
  "errors": [{"message": "generateKey does not support ECDSA"}]
}
```

The relevant call extracted from the delivered application JavaScript is:

```js
crypto.subtle.generateKey(
  { name: "ECDSA", namedCurve: "P-256", hash: { name: "SHA-256" } },
  false,
  ["sign", "verify"]
);
```

This snippet documents the site's actual call; the end-to-end site reproduction above was tested, rather than a separate standalone CLI invocation of this snippet.

## Evidence and failure boundary

- Main document and application scripts return HTTP 200.
- The application's DPoP helper awaits ECDSA key generation. An asynchronous request interceptor awaits the proof before sending the API request.
- The profile hook wraps the failure as the APIError above and throws it into the React error boundary.
- No `/users/get_profile` or product-list request appears in the captured network events. There is therefore no failed product API HTTP status to report: the failure occurs before transmission.
- The page eventually displays `ページの読み込みに失敗しました` (page loading failed).
- Reproduced in three diagnostic runs. JavaScript and React execute far enough to reach the application error boundary; this is not a complete hydration failure.
- A separate Google advertising iframe throws an `onmessage`/transferred-port error. That is not the basis for this diagnosis; the independent Mercari error above identifies the request-preparation blocker.

## Expected behavior / requested scope

Support standards-compatible ECDSA P-256 key generation and the associated public-key JWK export / ECDSA signing operations needed by DPoP clients. Regression coverage should test actual key generation and signature behavior, not just API presence.

Implementing key generation alone may reveal further compatibility blockers; this report does not claim that ECDSA support alone will make all of Mercari work. No workaround that skips proof generation or substitutes fake cryptographic output is requested.

## Current main source check

Main at `8343955f15ed717b7718c86deb72f676c9ebfe06` was inspected, not built or runtime-tested. In `crates/obscura-js/js/bootstrap.js`, `generateKey` handles HMAC and AES algorithms, then throws:

```js
throw new DOMException("generateKey does not support " + alg.name, "NotSupportedError");
```

Thus the same unsupported branch remains in current main source.

## Headless Chrome comparison

A fresh paired Chrome test was not performed for this report. The diagnosis is grounded in the captured application error, request interceptor code, absent outgoing seller API requests, and the matching unsupported branch in Obscura's implementation.

Raw headers, cookies, tracking identifiers, and full network dumps are intentionally omitted.

1. Render any page containing nested flexbox containers or HTML5 `<dialog>` elements where container dimensions are governed by intrinsic child contents (e.g. `min-height: auto` or flex items without explicit fixed pixel heights).
2. Inspect computed styles or capture viewport screenshots:
```bash
obscura fetch "https://www.linkedin.com/feed/?shareActive=true" --screenshot modal.png
```
3. Evaluate computed dimensions of the modal `<dialog>` and inner containers:
```javascript
(() => {
  const d = document.querySelector('dialog');
  const s = window.getComputedStyle(d);
  return { width: s.width, height: s.height, display: s.display };
})()
```
Output:
```json
{
  "display": "flex",
  "width": "800px",
  "height": "0px"
}
```
Similarly, child flex containers within feed cards collapse to `width: 3px`, causing enclosed text to wrap vertically into single-character columns.

### Expected behavior
Flex containers with intrinsic or auto sizing should measure their flex children and expand to accommodate their rendered content. `<dialog>` elements displayed as `flex` should resolve positive bounding heights.

Nested flex containers collapse to `height: 0px` (or `width: 3px`). Even when `<dialog>` has `open` set to true, the element renders as an empty 0-height box, obscuring all nested form controls and action buttons unless explicit CSS pixel overrides are manually injected.

items.title: innerHTML/textContent/subtree removal leaks native external_stylesheets entries for removed <link>s
items.body:
### Summary

Removing a subtree that contains a `<link rel="stylesheet">` does not release the element's **native** `external_stylesheets` entry, so the native CSS state grows unbounded on SPAs that swap content.

The native entry (registered via `op_external_stylesheet_set` and tracked in `_linkedStylesheetNodes`) is only released in `Node.removeChild`, and only for the **directly** removed node (`_linkedStylesheetNodes.has(c)`). Subtree removals never reach it:
- `element.innerHTML = ...` (and `textContent = ...`) remove children through a native path and only detach `<style>`/`<link>` *JS wrapper* state (`_detachStyleSheetsInSubtree`), never the native entry.
- `removeChild(ancestor)` releases only the ancestor's own entry, not descendant `<link>`s'.

Introduced when CSS moved from synthetic `<style>` elements to native DOM state (04418a5); the cleanup path was not extended.

### Trigger

An SPA that repeatedly does `container.innerHTML = '<link rel="stylesheet" href="...">...'` (or swaps a subtree containing stylesheet links) accumulates a native `external_stylesheets` entry per removed `<link>` that is never freed.

### Fix

Release the native entry (`op_external_stylesheet_remove` + `_linkedStylesheetNodes.delete`) for every `<link>` in a removed subtree: fold it into `_detachStyleSheetsInSubtree` (covers removeChild/replaceChild/textContent/replaceChildren) and add it to the `innerHTML` setter.

### Affected
- `crates/obscura-js/js/bootstrap.js` — `_detachStyleSheetsInSubtree`, the `innerHTML` setter

Two DOM/Canvas correctness bugs in bootstrap.js: stroke() is a no-op and innerText is aliased to textContent
items.body:
Hi! We have been evaluating Obscura as a rendering engine and hit two bugs in
`crates/obscura-js/js/bootstrap.js`. Both are self-contained, both have a fix we
have been running locally for a few weeks, and we would be happy to send PRs if
you agree with the approach. Opening this first as CONTRIBUTING.md asks.

## 1. `CanvasRenderingContext2D.stroke()` draws nothing, and gradients drop their stops

`stroke()` is literally `stroke() {}`, and `createLinearGradient()` returns an
object whose `addColorStop()` is also empty, so every stop is discarded.

The practical effect is that anything drawn with outlines disappears: line
charts, area charts, and every axis. On a chart-heavy dashboard we render for
testing, the page differed from Chrome on **32.35%** of pixels. With the fix
below, the same page differs on **1.16%**, and the primitives that already
worked (fills, arcs, clearRect) are unchanged.

What the fix does:
- implements `stroke()` over the existing path representation, honouring
  `lineWidth` and `strokeStyle`;
- makes `addColorStop()` actually record stops, and interpolates them for
  linear gradients;
- also fixes polygon `fill()`, which had the same "path is collected but never
  rasterised" shape.

## 2. `innerText` returns source text, including `<script>` bodies and hidden subtrees

`get innerText() { return this.textContent; }`

`innerText` is the *rendered* text; `textContent` is the source. Aliasing them
returns everything the user cannot see: the full body of every `<script>` and
`<style>` element, plus `display:none` / `[hidden]` subtrees.

Measured on `github.com/topics`: `innerText` returns **1.3 MB** where a browser
returns **5.5 KB**, and almost all of the difference is JavaScript source.

This matters beyond correctness for anyone driving Obscura from an agent: text
extracted this way gets fed to a language model, and that 1.3 MB is paid for in
tokens on every page read.

What the fix does: walks the tree instead of aliasing, skipping never-rendered
elements (`SCRIPT`, `STYLE`, `HEAD`, `TEMPLATE`, …), honouring `display:none`,
`visibility:hidden` and `[hidden]` via `getComputedStyle`, and inserting the
line breaks that block boundaries imply. Layout-dependent details
(`text-transform`, overflow clipping) are deliberately out of scope: it only
uses the CSS the engine already computes.

## Testing

Both fixes are exercised by standalone harnesses that extract the patched
classes from `bootstrap.js` and run them without a Rust build (~200 ms):
14 assertions for canvas, 12 for `innerText`. On the unpatched tree of `cf26f45`
the canvas harness is 6 passed / 8 failed; with the fix, 14 / 0.

We can port these into whatever test layout you prefer for the PRs, or drop them
if you would rather cover this differently. Happy to split into two PRs (one per
bug) or send one, whichever is easier for you to review.

items.title: HTML element interfaces are aliases of Element, so every brand check matches: style-loader cannot install any stylesheet
items.body:
## Summary

Most HTML element interfaces are aliases of `Element` in `bootstrap.js` (`globalThis.HTMLIFrameElement = Element;`, and 34 more). Web IDL gives each interface its own brand, so `div instanceof HTMLIFrameElement` must be `false`; with the alias it is `true` for every element and every interface. Any feature detection keyed on a brand therefore takes the wrong branch.

The concrete casualty is webpack's **style-loader**, which cannot install a single stylesheet. `style-loader/lib/addStyles.js` resolves its insert target and then checks whether that target is an iframe:

```js
var styleTarget = document.querySelector(target);   // <head>
if (styleTarget instanceof window.HTMLIFrameElement) {   // true on obscura
  try { styleTarget = styleTarget.contentDocument.head } catch (e) { styleTarget = null }
}
memo[selector] = styleTarget;   // null, cached
...
if (!target) throw new Error("Couldn't find a style target. This probably means that the value for the 'insertInto' parameter is invalid.");
```

`<head>` is reported as an iframe, `head.contentDocument` throws, the `catch` caches `null`, and every subsequent style insertion fails with that message. So a webpack-built application renders with no CSS at all.

This is the same class of bug as the `HTMLSlotElement` comment already in `bootstrap.js` ("with `HTMLSlotElement = Element` every element was an instance, but `assignedElements()` did not exist … threw a TypeError on a plain `<div>`"), for the rest of the surface.

## Reproduction

```bash
obscura fetch --eval "JSON.stringify({headIsIframe: document.head instanceof HTMLIFrameElement, divIsAnchor: document.createElement('div') instanceof HTMLAnchorElement, inputIsSelect: document.createElement('input') instanceof HTMLSelectElement, headCtor: document.head.constructor.name, divCtor: document.createElement('div').constructor.name})" https://example.com
```

Obscura v0.2.2 (x86_64-linux release):

```json
{"headIsIframe":true,"divIsAnchor":true,"inputIsSelect":true,"headCtor":"Element","divCtor":"Element"}
```

Chrome 151.0.7922.34:

```json
{"headIsIframe":false,"divIsAnchor":false,"inputIsSelect":false,"headCtor":"HTMLHeadElement","divCtor":"HTMLDivElement"}
```

The prototype chain differs the same way — obscura: `Element → Node → Object`; Chrome: `HTMLHeadElement → HTMLElement → Element → Node → EventTarget → Object`.

## Real-world impact

A production Angular + AngularJS console (webpack-built, style-loader in the bundle) went from unusable to fully rendered once brands answer per spec. Same commit, same page, only this fix applied on top of #1000:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| DOM nodes | 33 | 151 |
| form controls found | 0 | 3 (email, password, checkbox) |
| `document.body.innerText` | empty | the real sign-in copy |
| screenshot | blank | correct, branded, laid out |
| `Couldn't find a style target` | thrown | gone |

The Playwright locator layer becomes usable on that page as a result: `page.fill()` and `locator.click()` on the sign-in form now resolve and dispatch instead of timing out on actionability.

## Proposed fix

Give each aliased interface a real brand while leaving element construction untouched:

- Keep `Element.prototype` as the interface prototype, so `HTMLDivElement.prototype.foo = …` still patches the prototype real elements use, exactly as the alias did.
- Answer `instanceof` from `Symbol.hasInstance` against the interface's tag names (and the XHTML namespace).
- Skip any interface that is already a real subclass (`globalThis[name] !== Element`), so `HTMLFormElement`, `HTMLTextAreaElement`, `HTMLSlotElement`, `HTMLImageElement` and the media elements are untouched — and so this stays correct if one of the others grows behaviour later.

An interface that needs *behaviour* deserves a real subclass plus an `_elementClassFor` entry, as `HTMLSlotElement` has. These 33 need only *identity*, and identity is fixable without touching `_wrap`/`_elementClassFor` or the renderer.

`HTMLElement` and `HTMLUnknownElement` are deliberately left as they are: the first matches every HTML element (`Element` is the closest approximation available here), and the second matches exactly the tags no other interface claims, which needs the full known-element list rather than a tag list of its own.

I have this working with tests, all four release configurations building, and the obstacle course unchanged; PR to follow.

## Environment

- Obscura v0.2.2 release binary and `main` @ `4b70288`
- Linux x86_64
- Playwright 1.62.1 via `chromium.connectOverCDP`
- Chrome 151.0.7922.34 as the reference browser

items.title: CL search pages: browser UA gets JS shell that never hydrates under V8
items.body:
# CL search pages: browser UA gets JS shell that never hydrates under V8

## Summary

Craigslist serves two different responses for the same URL depending on the client's User-Agent:

- **Non-browser UAs** (curl, node fetch, no UA): full server-rendered HTML with all listings embedded in the page. ~14 KB.
- **Browser UAs** (Chrome/145, Obscura's default): a lightweight JS shell (~2.4 KB) that requires client-side hydration to populate results.

Obscura identifies as `Chrome/145.0.0.0`, so CL serves the browser version. But the hydration step never completes under V8 — results stay at "retrieving..." → "no results found" regardless of wait time.

## Reproduction

```bash
# This works (server-rendered, listings in HTML):
curl -s "https://www.craigslist.org/search/area/scranton?cat=sss&query=iphone" | grep -c "iPhone 17promax"
# → 3

# This fails (browser shell, no hydration under V8):
obscura fetch "https://www.craigslist.org/search/area/scranton?cat=sss&query=iphone" \
  --wait 12 \
  --eval "document.querySelectorAll('.cl-search-result').length"
# → 0

# Same URL in real Chrome: 60 results render fine.
```

## Tested variants (all fail)

| Variant | Result |
|---------|--------|
| `--wait 8` / `--wait 12` | 0 results |
| `--wait-until networkidle0 --wait 5` | navigation timeout at 30s |
| `--wait-until load --wait 12` | 0 results |
| `-stealth` build | 0 results |
| `OBSCURA_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=15000` | 0 results |
| CDP serve mode + external client | "No page for session" |

## Root cause hypothesis

CL's hydration JS likely depends on a Blink-specific API or behavior that standalone V8 doesn't replicate. The page loads, JS executes, but the XHR that fetches/populates results never completes. In Chrome (Blink + V8) the same page hydrates in <2s.

## Suggested fix

One of:
1. **Add a `--no-browser-ua` or `--plain-fetch` flag** to `obscura fetch` that skips the browser engine and does a plain HTTP GET (like curl), returning the server-rendered HTML. This would work for CL and similar sites that serve full content to non-browser clients.
2. **Allow overriding the User-Agent** so CL serves the server-rendered version instead of the JS shell.
3. **Fix V8 hydration** for CL's specific pattern (if it's a known gap).

Option 1 is the most broadly useful — many sites serve full content to non-browser clients and only gate behind JS for real browsers.

## Environment

- Obscura 0.2.2, Linux x86_64
- Test URL: `https://www.craigslist.org/search/area/scranton?cat=sss&query=iphone`
- V8-Version reported by Obscura: 14.5.0.0

## Environment

Obscura **v0.2.2**, official Linux x86_64 render-enabled archive, stealth off; Arch Linux, kernel `7.2.3-arch1-3`. Native MCP over stdio.

## Minimal fixture

Create `index.html` in an empty directory:

```html
<!doctype html>
<button id="open">Open dialog</button>
<dialog id="dialog"><input id="field"><button id="close">Request close</button></dialog>
<script>
window.cancels = 0;
const dialog = document.querySelector('#dialog');
document.querySelector('#open').onclick = () => {
  dialog.showModal();
  document.querySelector('#field').focus();
};
dialog.addEventListener('cancel', () => window.cancels++);
document.querySelector('#close').onclick = () => dialog.requestClose();
</script>
```

Serve that directory:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1
```

## MCP calls

MCP client launch command (fresh session):

```sh
obscura mcp --allow-private-network
```

Invoke these MCP tools in order:

| Tool | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `browser_navigate` | `{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:8765/"}` |
| `browser_click` | `{"selector":"#open"}` |
| `browser_evaluate` | `{"expression":"JSON.stringify({open:document.querySelector('#dialog').open,active:document.activeElement?.id,cancels:window.cancels})"}` |
| `browser_press_key` | `{"key":"Escape","selector":"#field"}` |
| `browser_evaluate` | `{"expression":"JSON.stringify({open:document.querySelector('#dialog').open,cancels:window.cancels})"}` |
| `browser_click` | `{"selector":"#close"}` |
| `browser_evaluate` | `{"expression":"JSON.stringify({open:document.querySelector('#dialog').open,cancels:window.cancels})"}` |

## Expected and actual

For a browser key press representing user input, Escape would request closure of the active modal: fire `cancel` and, unless prevented, close the dialog.

Actual observations:

| Point | State |
| --- | --- |
| Before Escape | `{"open":true,"active":"field","cancels":0}` |
| After Escape | `{"open":true,"cancels":0}` |
| After the Request close button | `{"open":false,"cancels":1}` |

**Control:** the same HTML with agent-browser 0.37.1 and headless Chromium 152.0.7977.82 closes on `press Escape`: `open=false`, `cancels=1`.

## Scope question

[`tool_press_key`](https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura/blob/v0.2.2/crates/obscura-mcp/src/lib.rs#L1061-L1085) implements its documented event-dispatch contract. This is a request for native Escape close-request behavior through automation, not for arbitrary synthetic DOM events to gain native default actions.

A trusted-marked, cancelable Escape keydown matching Obscura's CDP event shape also left the dialog open. Source inspection points to a missing Escape-to-close-request binding; CDP itself was not runtime-tested.

Is this close-request behavior in scope, and if so, should it live in shared browser input handling rather than an MCP-specific special case?

---

AI tools assisted with investigating this issue and preparing the report.

items.title: DDoS-Guard challenge still doesn't complete after #285 fix (stealth render)
items.body:
## Summary

`--stealth` render of a DDoS-Guard-protected page (`annas-archive.gl`) still returns the unsolved challenge page rather than the destination content, even with the #285/#286 `insertAdjacentText`/`insertAdjacentElement` polyfill fix present in the build (verified — see below). The challenge no longer crashes, but it also doesn't complete within a normal wait window.

## Environment

- Binary: `target/release/obscura.exe`, built 2026-08-24/26
- Confirmed `38fa859` (fix #285/#286) is an ancestor of the build's HEAD (`f449e6f`)
- Command:
  ```
  obscura fetch "https://annas-archive.gl/search?q=<query>" --dump html --wait-until networkidle0 --stealth --timeout 20
  ```

## What comes back

First ~500 bytes of the response:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html><head><title>DDoS-Guard</title><meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/.well-known/ddos-guard/js-challenge/index.css">
<style data-obscura-external-stylesheets="">*{margin:0;padding:0}html,body{
font-family:"DejaVu Sans","Segoe UI","Roboto","Courier New","Verdana","Arial","Helvetica";
height:100%;color:#333}#ddg-img-loading{animation:move 1s infinite linear}
@keyframes move{0%{transform:rotate(0deg)}...
```

Total response length 4734 bytes — this is the challenge page itself (loading-spinner state, `/.well-known/ddos-guard/js-challenge/` stylesheet), not the destination content and not a crash. `--wait-until networkidle0` with a 20s timeout isn't enough for it to resolve and redirect.

## What I don't know yet, worth checking

I haven't confirmed what DDoS-Guard actually needs past this point for this specific site config — could be:
- A longer settle time before the redirect fires (worth trying a longer `--timeout` / different `--wait-until` first, cheapest thing to rule out)
- Another missing DOM/Web API in the challenge script, same class of issue as #285 (worth diffing against a real Chrome devtools console on the same URL for thrown errors)
- A secondary visual challenge. DDoS-Guard is known to escalate to a distorted-character image puzzle (several characters, varying colour/size/rotation, arranged non-overlapping) when the JS auto-challenge doesn't clear a fingerprint check — I haven't verified that's what's happening here, since the captured output is still the loading-spinner state, not a rendered puzzle. If it does escalate to that, it's not something a JS/DOM polyfill fixes at all — it needs an actual solve step.

## Possible direction for the visual-challenge case

If/when it does turn out to be a rendered image puzzle rather than a pure JS timing issue, a `--dump screenshot` + vision-model OCR pass (read back the distorted characters, submit the answer) would be a plausible fallback path — same shape as existing CAPTCHA-handling patterns in the Playwright/Selenium ecosystem, just backed by a vision LLM instead of a classical OCR model, which tends to handle rotation/colour/size variation and non-overlapping distorted glyphs better than traditional OCR. Flagging as a direction, not a confirmed diagnosis — happy to help narrow down which of the three cases above it actually is if that's useful; I have a live repro at hand (rtorrent-mcp's Anna's Archive mirror search, which is what surfaced this).

items.title: cdp: Input.dispatch* commands are not read while a page-triggered navigation (Enter submit, link click) loads; the next command times out
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate (#890 is about layout opening its own HTTP requests; this is about the connection processor not reading commands while a JS/form-triggered navigation loads).
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main` (reproduced with the v0.2.2 stealth release binary and with `main` at 727cc46).
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability.

### obscura version or commit

v0.2.2 (`a1e09de6`) and `main` 727cc46

### OS and architecture

Debian 13 x86_64

### How are you using obscura?

CDP server with an own CDP client (Puppeteer/Playwright-style command sequences)

### Affected area

CDP server / input handling / navigation

### Build variant

Render-enabled with stealth (`--features render,stealth`); the code path is feature-independent

### Stealth mode

On (`--stealth`), not relevant to the behaviour

### Reproduction

When a CDP command makes the page schedule a document navigation, the navigation runs inline on the connection processor and nothing is read from the connection until the new document has loaded:

- `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` `keyDown` Enter in a `<form method=get>` field: the command is answered, then `process_cdp_message` runs `check_pending_navigation` and dispatches the synthetic `Page.navigate` inline (`crates/obscura-cdp/src/server.rs`, `process_cdp_message`). The client's next command (the matching `keyUp`) is not read until the result page is fetched and loaded.
- `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` `mouseReleased` on a link or submit button: the handler itself awaits `page.process_pending_navigation()` (`crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/input.rs`), so the `mouseReleased` response is delayed by the whole navigation.

Chromium answers both input commands in milliseconds and dispatches the input to the outgoing document; the navigation loads while the client keeps sending commands. With Obscura a client that uses a per-command timeout (Puppeteer's default protocol timeout, or a scraper's per-action budget) times out whenever the target page needs longer than that timeout, although nothing is wrong with the page.

Minimal reproduction (offline, one local HTTP server that answers `/slow` after 1.5 s):

1. `Page.navigate` to `<form method=get action=/slow><input id=q name=q></form>`, wait for load.
2. `Runtime.evaluate` `document.getElementById('q').focus()`.
3. `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` `{type: keyDown, key: Enter, code: Enter, windowsVirtualKeyCode: 13}` — answered immediately.
4. `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` `{type: keyUp, ...}` — answered only after ~1.5 s (after the `/slow` document loaded). With a 10 s server delay and an 8 s client timeout the `keyUp` times out.

Same with `<a href=/slow>`: `mousePressed` is immediate, `mouseReleased` returns after the navigation.

### Expected behavior

Input commands sent while a page-scheduled navigation is in flight are answered at once (Chromium timing), the navigation loads in the background through the same deferral loop that `Page.navigate` already uses, and the frame events (`Page.frameStartedNavigating`, `Page.frameNavigated`, ...) are emitted from there.

### Actual behavior

The connection is not read until the navigation finished; the next command waits for the full document fetch.

### Logs / additional context

`Runtime.evaluate` / `Runtime.callFunctionOn` have the same inline `process_pending_navigation` in `crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/runtime.rs`; a navigation started from an evaluated expression still blocks that command (out of scope for the first fix, mentioned for completeness).

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

items.title: Synchronous XMLHttpRequest never issues the request: open(..., false) is ignored and status stays 0
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability.

### obscura version or commit

`main` (also reproduces on the published v0.2.2 macOS arm64 archives, stealth and non-stealth)

### OS and architecture

macOS arm64

### How are you using obscura?

CDP server (`obscura serve`), driven over `Runtime.evaluate`.

### Affected area

JavaScript: `XMLHttpRequest` synchronous mode.

### Build variant

Render-enabled.

### Stealth mode

Both off and on — identical results.

### Reproduction

```js
const x = new XMLHttpRequest();
x.open('GET', '/some/path', false);   // async = false
x.send();
x.status;         // Chrome: the real status  |  obscura: 0
x.responseText;   // Chrome: the body         |  obscura: ''
```

Measured against a real host:

| request | Chrome | obscura |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sync GET, missing path | `status 404`, 1312 bytes | **`status 0`, 0 bytes** |
| sync GET, existing asset | `status 200`, 13594 bytes | **`status 0`, 0 bytes** |

No exception is raised and no `error` event distinguishes it from a genuine
network failure — `send()` simply returns with the request never issued.

### Expected behavior

`send()` returns only after the exchange completes, with `status`,
`responseText`, `readyState` and the response headers populated, as Chrome does.

### Actual behavior

`XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open` ignores its third argument entirely
(`open(method, url, async_)` never reads `async_`), and `send()` always goes
through the async `fetch` path. A synchronous caller therefore reads `status 0`
on the line after `send()`.

### Does headless Chrome behave the same?

No — Chrome performs the request synchronously.

### Why it matters

Sync XHR is deprecated but still specified outside a Worker, and real apps use
it exactly where async is not an option: reading bootstrap configuration before
the rest of the app is constructed. A silent `status 0` is worse than an
exception, because callers treat it as "the server said no" and take an error
branch that then poisons everything downstream.

I hit this on a production SPA whose config loader does

```js
xhr.open('GET', '/static/customSetting/customSetting.json', false);
xhr.send();
if (xhr.status === 200) { /* … */ } else { window.someErrorFlag = true; }
```

Chrome gets a real 404 and takes the normal fallback; obscura gets `status 0`
and sets the error flag, which changes the API base URL the app uses from then
on.

### Willing to work on it

I have a working patch (a dedicated blocking op so the isolate is not
re-entered while the request is in flight) and will open a PR referencing this
issue.

items.title: fetch() omits the default Referer on same-origin requests
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability.

### Environment

v0.2.2, macOS arm64, official render-enabled stealth archive, Playwright over CDP. Reproduces with `--stealth` both off and on. Headless Chrome 152 sends the expected header.

### Reproduction

Run `obscura serve --allow-private-network`, then this Python script (requires Playwright):

```python
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        body = repr(self.headers.get('Referer')).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/html')
        self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)
    def log_message(self, *args): pass

server = HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Handler)
threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp('http://127.0.0.1:9222')
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto(f'http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/')
    print(page.evaluate("fetch('/echo').then(r => r.text())"))
    browser.close()
server.shutdown()
```

### Expected and actual

The same-origin request should carry the document URL as its Referer. Chrome returns `'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/'`; Obscura returns `None`. This is the header received by the server, not a CDP reporting difference.

### Related work

Closed, unmerged PRs #128 and #446 included automatic Referer handling. The JS fetch path still omits it in v0.2.2 and the code on main `a1e09de`. I have a local fix with tests for default and explicit referrer policies and intend to submit a focused follow-up after feedback.

## Summary `Page.printToPDF` produces a PDF whose page content is a single **JPEG image** rather than vector drawing operations against embedded fonts. The output therefore has **no text layer at all** — nothing can be selected, copied, searched or read by a screen reader — and page resolution is hard-capped at 800 px wide (≈97 DPI at A4) regardless of `scale` or `deviceScaleFactor`. Pagination, page size and visual layout are all correct. This is specifically about how page content is encoded. ## Environment - `h4ckf0r0day/obscura:latest`, banner reports `Headless Browser v0.2.2` - digest `sha256:4f915617741d2e7cd5fac6dd03592c10ca2653d37d9ac53c8224a621af874197`, linux/amd64 - client: `puppeteer-core@23` - host: Linux x86_64, Docker ## Repro ```bash docker run -d --name obscura-repro -p 9333:9222 h4ckf0r0day/obscura mkdir obscura-repro && cd obscura-repro && npm init -y && npm install puppeteer-core@23 ``` `repro.js`: ```js const fs = require("fs"); const puppeteer = require("puppeteer-core"); (async () => { const browser = await puppeteer.connect({ browserWSEndpoint: "ws://localhost:9333/devtools/browser" }); const page = await browser.newPage(); await page.setContent("

Hello

RM 6,000.00

"); const bytes = await page.pdf({ format: "A4", printBackground: true }); fs.writeFileSync("out.pdf", Buffer.from(bytes)); await page.close(); await browser.disconnect(); })(); ``` ```bash node repro.js pdffonts out.pdf pdftotext out.pdf - | wc -c pdfimages -list out.pdf ``` ## Actual vs expected The same HTML through obscura 0.2.2 and through Chrome headless (puppeteer 22, `Skia/PDF m127`): | | Chrome headless | obscura 0.2.2 | |---|---|---| | file size | 12,368 B | 16,933 B | | `pdffonts` | `AAAAAA+LiberationSans-Bold`, `BAAAAA+LiberationSans` — CID TrueType, embedded, subsetted | *(no rows — zero fonts)* | | `pdftotext out.pdf - \| wc -c` | `20` | `1` | | `pdfimages -list` | *(no rows — no raster)* | `1 0 image 800 600 rgb 3 8 jpeg no 5 0 97 97 15.8K 1.1%` | Expected: text emitted as `Tj`/`TJ` operators against embedded font subsets, matching Chrome's `Page.printToPDF`. ## Resolution is capped, and `scale` makes it worse Setting both `page.setViewport({ deviceScaleFactor })` and `page.pdf({ scale })`: | requested scale | raster | effective DPI | |---|---|---| | 1 | 800 × 600 JPEG | 97 | | 2 | 800 × 566 JPEG | **48** | | 3 | rejected: `Protocol error (Page.printToPDF): Invalid parameters: scale must be between 0.1 and 2` | — | So `scale` is validated but does not increase raster resolution — at `scale: 2` the effective DPI roughly halves. `deviceScaleFactor` has no effect on the raster either. There appears to be no way for a client to raise output quality above ~97 DPI. ## What does work Pagination and geometry are correct, so the layout/paging side of `printToPDF` looks sound. 120 short `

` elements: ``` Pages: 4 Page size: 595.274 x 841.889 pts (A4) page num type width height color comp bpc enc ... x-ppi y-ppi size 1 0 image 800 1132 rgb 3 8 jpeg 97 97 46.2K 2 1 image 800 1132 rgb 3 8 jpeg 97 97 47.3K 3 2 image 800 1132 rgb 3 8 jpeg 97 97 48.0K 4 3 image 800 702 rgb 3 8 jpeg 97 97 31.7K ``` Every page is its own JPEG, correctly broken and correctly sized — only the encoding of page content is the problem. ## Impact This rules obscura out for server-side document generation (payslips, invoices, statements, tax forms), which is otherwise a strong fit — in our testing obscura rendered a real document pixel-accurately and **6× faster than bundled Chromium** (148 ms vs 938 ms end to end), in a 91 MB image instead of a Chromium install plus its shared-library dependencies. The blockers for that use case are: 1. **No text layer** — recipients cannot select, copy or search figures; screen readers get nothing; downstream text extraction and PDF/A-style archival are impossible. 2. **~97 DPI lossy raster** — these documents get printed, and JPEG-compressed text at 97 DPI is visibly soft with ringing artifacts around glyph edges. 3. **File size grows with page area** rather than with text content (132 KB vs 60 KB for one real single-page document). Point 1 is the hard one; 2 and 3 would mostly follow from fixing it. ## Suggestion Emit vector text with embedded (subsetted) font programs, as Chrome's Skia PDF backend does. If a vector text path is a large piece of work, an interim `deviceScaleFactor`/`scale`-honouring raster at 2–3× would at least make printed output acceptable, though it would not restore selectable text. Happy to test a build against a real multi-page document if that's useful.
