items.title: Feature: Chrome extension support (adblock/tracker-blocking first) for agent workflows
items.body:
## Feature: Chrome extension support (adblock, session managers, privacy tools)

**Why this matters for Obscura's core use case (AI agents + scraping):**
Obscura's pitch is a lightweight agent browser, but agent workflows constantly need extension functionality that today requires a full Chromium:

1. **Ad/tracker blocking** — uBlock Origin / AdGuard. Agents scraping content sites get junk-filled DOMs (ads, cookie banners, trackers) that bloat snapshots, inflate token counts, and break selectors. A native adblock is the #1 quality-of-life gap vs headless Chrome + extensions.
2. **Session/cookie managers** — extensions that persist/restore auth state across agent runs (the #694/#629 persistence work overlaps but extensions are the ecosystem answer).
3. **Privacy/consent tools** — I don't care about tracking (self-hosted, TOR, anti-detection), cookie auto-consent, etc.
4. **Site-specific integrations** — agents hitting sites that require an extension (e.g. wallet bridges, captcha helpers, enterprise SSO helpers) are blocked entirely without extension support.

**The gap:** Chromium-based agents get all of this for free via the extension ecosystem. Obscura (independent engine) currently has no extension host, so every one of these needs reimplementing natively or is impossible.

**Proposed direction (open to maintainers' thoughts):**
- Even a **minimal MV2/MV3 extension host** (background/service worker + declarativeNetRequest for adblocking) would cover the top use case (ad/tracker blocking) without full extension API parity
- declarativeNetRequest alone would let uBlock-style filter lists work without a full extension runtime
- Longer term: content-script injection + extension messaging for the session-manager class

**Related:** #527 (fingerprint surface), #694 (persistent profiles), #629 (MCP storage) — extension support would complement all three.

Happy to help test or contribute if there's appetite. (Context: I'm a Hermes-agent user who hit Obscura's CDP gaps — see my rebase of #634 — and extension support is the biggest remaining reason I keep Chromium as my agent browser.)

items.title: `fetch_file_url` has no `--allow-file-access` gate of its own; the check lives only in its callers
items.body:
**Version:** `main` at `a1e09de`, also v0.2.2. All build configurations.

**The shape.** `fetch_file_url` in `crates/obscura-net/src/client.rs` reads whatever path it is handed. The `--allow-file-access` check lives entirely in the callers: CDP's `Page.navigate` and `Target.createTarget` via `util::url_is_file_scheme`, and `subresource_allowed` in obscura-browser. The invariant therefore holds only as long as every future call site remembers it. That is the shape of GHSA-q55h-vfv9-qcr5 and its incomplete-fix variant: a decision enforced at N call sites gets enforced at N-1 sooner or later.

**To be straight:** I found no exploitable path that ships today. This is defence in depth, not a live hole.

**Proposal.** Make `allow_file_access` a required parameter of `fetch_file_url`, so a caller has to state that reading local files is intended, and a field on both HTTP clients defaulting to false. `BrowserContext` assigns the flag after the client is inside an `Arc`, so it needs interior mutability, and `BrowserContext::set_allow_file_access` should set the context flag and the client's together so the two copies cannot drift. `obscura fetch file://...` opts in explicitly, since a local operator running the CLI against their own filesystem is a different trust boundary from a CDP client over a socket. A closed gate should report the gate, not "no such file", or the refusal becomes a probe for which paths exist.

Not in scope, and worth separate issues if wanted: path-root confinement, and blocking file-to-file subresources the way Chrome does without `--allow-file-access-from-files` (a behaviour change to a documented local-testing workflow).

I have this implemented with 5 tests. PR to follow if the direction suits.

items.title: `--allow-private-network` is all-or-nothing; a scoped `--allow-network <CIDR>` would keep the metadata endpoints closed
items.body:
**Version:** `main` at `a1e09de`, also v0.2.2. All build configurations.

**The problem.** `--allow-private-network` (and `OBSCURA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK=1`) is the only escape hatch from the SSRF deny-set, and it disables the deny-set entirely: loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, CGNAT, and with them the cloud metadata endpoints `169.254.169.254` and `100.100.100.200`. It is also the flag an operator must set to test an internal application. So the common case, "point Obscura at my app on 10.20.x.y", also hands every page that app loads an unrestricted internal pivot, metadata credentials included.

**Proposal.** `--allow-network 10.20.0.0/16` (repeatable, comma-separated, `OBSCURA_ALLOW_NETWORK` equivalent) that exempts exactly what is named and leaves the rest denied. `is_forbidden_ip` stays the single definition of the deny-set; the policy only relaxes it, never tightens it, so it remains an escape hatch rather than a firewall an operator might mistake it for. Applies to both transports; #831 already threaded the blanket flag into the stealth client, and the scoped list layers on top of that seed without changing its signature.

Details worth deciding up front: a hostname carries no address, so `localhost` cannot be judged against an allowlist before resolution and the decision defers to the DNS-time guard; `::ffff:a.b.c.d` should match a v4 prefix, mirroring the deny-set's own unwrapping; a malformed prefix should be a startup error rather than a silent skip; a `/0` entry should warn.

I have this implemented (hand-rolled CIDR parsing, about 40 lines, to avoid a new dependency and a `deny.toml` review) with 6 integration and 13 unit tests. PR to follow if the direction suits.

items.title: Cookie store permissions are incidental and persistence failures are silent; control-plane routing matches substrings of the whole request head; `build.log` is committed
items.body:
**Version:** `main` at `a1e09de`, also v0.2.2. All build configurations.

Three small hygiene items that belong together in one PR.

**1. Cookie store permissions and silent failure.** `{storage-dir}/cookies.json` holds live session tokens in plaintext. Its permissions are incidental: `NamedTempFile` creates at 0600 and `persist` renames, so a fresh file happens to land right, but nothing checks it, nothing sets it when persisting over an existing file, and the directory keeps the umask default. Separately, `save_cookies` discards `create_dir_all`'s error with `let _ =` and logs the save failure at `warn!`, which produces no output in the CLI fetch path because no tracing subscriber is installed there. Repro: point `--storage-dir` at a directory the process cannot write; the run exits 0 and no `cookies.json` appears.

**2. Control-plane routing.** `accept_dispatch` in `crates/obscura-cdp/src/server.rs` routes on `head.contains("/json/list")` and friends, which matches anywhere in the request head including inside a header value. Repro: a WebSocket upgrade for `/devtools/page/page-1` that carries a header whose value contains `/json/list` is served the JSON target list instead of being upgraded. Nothing exploitable found; those endpoints expose no more than they already do to whoever can reach the port. The defect is the shape: routing on attacker-influenced bytes from anywhere in the head. Routing on the request target from the request line is a two-line change.

**3. `build.log` is committed.** It is a build transcript carrying an absolute path from the maintainer's machine (`/root/obscura2/merge471`). It should be removed and `*.log` ignored.

I have a fix ready for all three (0600/0700 set explicitly, `error!`-level reporting that says cookies will not be persisted, request-target routing with tests for the header-value case and the `/json/versionify` near-miss, `build.log` removed). PR to follow.

items.title: fix(js): interpolate console/release objectIds via js_string_literal (defense-in-depth)
items.body:
## Summary

`take_pending_runtime_events` and `release_object` in `crates/obscura-js/src/runtime.rs` interpolate object IDs into single-quoted JS strings without JSON-escaping, unlike the rest of the codebase which uses `js_string_literal` / `object_id_literal` (`serde_json::to_string`).

## Location

`crates/obscura-js/src/runtime.rs` — ~L1117/1120 (console/pending runtime events) and ~L2215/2218 (release_object).

## Assessment

**Not currently exploitable:** console IDs are generated by bootstrap.js with the shape `console-{frameId}-{counter}` (digits and hyphens only), and `release_object` is guarded by the object store's `remove()` succeeding, so only internally-generated keys ever reach these sites. This is a **defense-in-depth / consistency** fix so the pattern can't become a bug if ID shapes ever change.

## Fix direction

Route both interpolation sites through the existing `js_string_literal` helper (already used by set_platform/set_user_agent), embedding the id as a JSON literal instead of hand-splicing into single quotes.

## Severity

LOW — hardening / consistency; no working exploit.

## What happens
`inner_text` returns raw `<script>` (and similar non-rendered) source text interleaved with the visible content. In Chromium the same page's `inner_text` only contains rendered text.

Numbers from the same URL, same UA, both engines:

| page | obscura `inner_text` | Chromium `inner_text` |

```

## Why it matters
Any scraper doing keyword matching / regex extraction over `inner_text` gets poisoned by ~100x script noise (false keyword hits, false numeric matches). It also makes CDP parity checks (obscura vs chromium text diff) fail on otherwise-working pages.

The default stylesheet / rendering model likely isn't excluding `script`/`style` elements from text extraction — Chromium's `innerText` skips non-rendered elements by spec (it returns rendered text).

items.title: Web Workers: importScripts() not implemented -> Yahoo Finance app dies and redirects to /lookup
items.body:
## Environment
- obscura v0.2.1 (windows x86_64 stealth build) — also reproduced on a fresh `cargo build --release` of master @ 14ce517 (2026-09-04, default features)
- Windows 10 x64, `obscura serve --stealth -p 9222`, client = Playwright (Python) `chromium.connect_over_cdp`

## What works
Plain pages render fine (example.com, and http://www.aastocks.com/tc/stocks/analysis/stock-aafn/0005/0/hk-stock-news/1 loads with a correct title), and the Yahoo SSR HTML itself is served correctly — `obscura fetch --stealth` reports the right title `HSBC Holdings plc (0005.HK) Latest Stock News & Headlines - Yahoo Finance`.

## What breaks
Any page whose app needs a Web Worker that loads scripts via `importScripts()` fails its client-side boot. Concrete case — https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/0005.HK/news :

1. Yahoo's app resolves the quote symbol in a Web Worker that loads its protobuf dependency with `importScripts(...)`
2. Console shows:
   - `Worker error: protobuf is not defined` (repeated)
   - `Worker error: undefined is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator))`
3. The app then hard-redirects to `https://finance.yahoo.com/lookup/?s=0005.HK` ("Symbol Lookup from Yahoo Finance") and never recovers — I sampled `page.title()` every 5s for 40s, stuck on the lookup page permanently.

## Root-cause suspicion
Grepping the current master tree, `importScripts` has no implementation anywhere (`grep -rn "importScripts" crates` → 0 hits), so any worker that pulls libraries via `importScripts()` gets a ReferenceError for the imported globals. The `Worker` constructor itself is registered (runtime tests reference it), which is why this half-works: the worker starts, then dies on first `importScripts` call.

## Repro
```
obscura serve --stealth -p 9222
# then, from Playwright (or any CDP client):
browser = chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
page = browser.new_page()
page.goto("https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/0005.HK/news")
# title ends up "Symbol Lookup from Yahoo Finance" instead of the quote page
```

Notes: the same failure happens with the page-provided UA and with the native UA, so it is not a UA/fingerprint mismatch — Yahoo serves the correct SSR HTML either way. Disabling `--stealth` makes the page fail even earlier (navigation never settles, "load-delaying dynamic scripts still pending" until the 30s deadline).

Even a minimal `importScripts` that fetches + evals the script URLs in the worker's global scope would unblock this class of sites. Happy to test a fix branch.

items.title: fill/click/selectOption via Playwright CDP hang despite element reporting visible/enabled/editable
items.body:
Using Playwright's `chromium.connectOverCDP()` against Obscura's `serve` mode (built from source, commit `14da23ddc432eaf8de6a14b44037626ce6fd9415`, `--features render`), Playwright's actionability-gated interaction methods consistently time out:

```
page.fill: Timeout 8000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for element to be visible, enabled and editable
```

This happens reproducibly on every interactive element type tested (text/email/tel inputs, `<select>`, buttons), across two separate runs, against a real-world SPA form (not a synthetic repro). Direct queries via `page.evaluate()` on the same elements — `getBoundingClientRect()`, `isVisible()`-equivalent checks — report the elements as completely normal. A workaround setting DOM values and dispatching native `.click()` via `page.evaluate()` (bypassing Playwright's actionability-checked methods) works reliably.

Page navigation, network interception, and console access via the same CDP connection all work correctly — this appears specific to whatever Playwright's actionability polling loop depends on.

**Suspected mechanism** (from reading source, not confirmed via live tracing): `getBoxModel`/`getContentQuads` in `crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/dom.rs` (~lines 300-361) appear to fall back to a hardcoded placeholder quad (`[8,8,108,8,108,28,8,28]`) when `resolve_node_id`'s objectId→node lookup misses, rather than raising a CDP error the way Chrome does (`"Could not compute box model."`). Playwright's actionability check repeatedly re-reads an element's box across animation frames to confirm stability before acting — if node resolution intermittently hits this fallback, the box would never stabilize and the hit-test point would land outside the real element, matching the observed symptom exactly (timeout, no protocol-level error).

Could not confirm this with confidence without instrumenting a live repro. Happy to share a minimal reproduction case if useful.

**Environment:** macOS, Docker (multi-stage build from the repo's own Dockerfile), Playwright (Node), commit `14da23d`.

items.title: v0.2.1 serve: RSS leaks to ~2.3 GB with sustained 50-100% CPU on long-running CDP server
items.body:
### Summary

`obscura serve` (v0.2.1) running as a long-lived CDP server on macOS leaks memory aggressively: RSS grows from ~33 MB to **~2.3 GB within a few hours**, accompanied by **sustained 50–60% CPU** even when idle. Baseline RSS is ~15–20 MB right after launch.

### Environment

- Obscura version: **0.2.1** (`obscura --version`)
- macOS 26.3 (Tahoe), Apple Silicon (M5), 24 GB RAM
- Launch mode: `obscura serve --port 9222 --stealth --allow-private-network`, kept alive via launchd (KeepAlive)
- Usage: headless CDP browser for AI agent / web scraping workflows

### Observed memory curve (monitored every 4h, process PID 2817, single continuous run)

| Timestamp (CST) | RSS | CPU avg | CPU max |
|---|---|---|---|
| 08-31 00:01 | 32.8 MB | 0% | 0% |
| 08-31 04:00 | 32.9 MB | 0% | 0% |
| 08-31 08:00 | **2274 MB** | 58.4% | 99.9% |
| 08-31 12:00 | 2269 MB | 58.9% | 100% |
| 08-31 16:00 | 2278 MB | 50.2% | 100% |

Same symptom reproduced earlier: after ~5 days of uptime RSS reached 2.4 GB with 100% CPU. Restarting the process brings RSS back to ~15–20 MB immediately.

### Expected behavior

Idle headless browser should hold roughly constant memory; CPU should drop to ~0% when no pages are active.

### Impact

- On a 24 GB laptop the leaked 2.3 GB plus sustained 50–100% CPU causes fan spin-up and system slowdown.
- The leak appears to be event-driven (memory jumps quickly rather than growing linearly hour by hour), suggesting an unbounded accumulation — e.g. page/JS-runtime instances not being released after tab close, or a leaking CDP event handler.

### Local workaround

I have a watchdog that restarts the process hourly when RSS > 300 MB or CPU > 90%. It works but masks the underlying issue.

### Questions / hints for maintainers

- Are page contexts / JS runtime instances fully dropped when the last tab of a session is closed?
- Any known accumulation in the CDP event loop or stealth instrumentation while idle?

Happy to run with `RUST_LOG=debug` or provide more data if useful.

items.title: Emulation.setUserAgentOverride is a silent no-op, and Network.setUserAgentOverride drops acceptLanguage
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability (those go through SECURITY.md, not a public issue).

### obscura version or commit

`9326880` (main, 2026-08-30)

### OS and architecture

Reproduced in the Linux CI container (rustc 1.98, x86_64). The defect is in the dispatch layer and is not platform-specific.

### How are you using obscura?

CDP (Puppeteer / Playwright / raw WebSocket)

### Stealth mode

None (the code path is the same in both modes)

### Reproduction

Two unit tests against `main`, no network needed:

```rust
// crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/network.rs
handle("setUserAgentOverride",
       &json!({ "userAgent": "UA/1.0", "acceptLanguage": "de-DE,de;q=0.9" }),
       &mut ctx, &session_id).await.unwrap();
assert_eq!(*page.http_client.accept_language.read().await, "de-DE,de;q=0.9");

// crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/emulation.rs
handle("setUserAgentOverride",
       &json!({ "userAgent": "UA/2.0", "acceptLanguage": "fr-FR,fr;q=0.9" }),
       &mut ctx, &session_id).await.unwrap();
assert_eq!(*page.http_client.user_agent.read().await, "UA/2.0");
```

Both fail on `9326880`:

```
FAIL domains::network::tests::set_user_agent_override_applies_accept_language
     assertion `left == right` failed: acceptLanguage must reach the client
       left: "en-US,en;q=0.9"      <- the default, untouched
      right: "de-DE,de;q=0.9"

FAIL domains::emulation::tests::emulation_set_user_agent_override_is_applied
     2 tests run: 0 passed, 2 failed
```

The `Network` case shows the locale never leaving the dispatcher; the `Emulation` case shows the whole command doing nothing, user agent included. Both calls returned `{}` — success.

### Expected behavior

`setUserAgentOverride` carries `userAgent`, `acceptLanguage` and `platform`. A client that sets a locale should see it on the wire and in the page, the way `userAgent` already works — `Network.setUserAgentOverride` writes `http_client.user_agent`, and the next navigation seeds `navigator.userAgent` from that same field, so the two cannot drift.

### Actual behavior

**1. `Emulation.setUserAgentOverride` is a silent no-op.** The `Emulation` handler ends in a catch-all:

```rust
"setTouchEmulationEnabled" => Ok(json!({})),
_ => Ok(json!({})),
```

`setUserAgentOverride` is not one of its four arms, so it falls through, replies `{}` and applies nothing — not even the user agent. This is the spelling the CDP spec lists as current; `Network.setUserAgentOverride` is the deprecated one.

**2. `Network.setUserAgentOverride` discards `acceptLanguage` and `platform`:**

```rust
"setUserAgentOverride" => {
    let ua = params.get("userAgent").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
    if let Some(page) = ctx.get_session_page(session_id) {
        page.http_client.set_user_agent(ua).await;
    }
    Ok(json!({}))
}
```

**3. The plumbing for the locale half already exists and is wired to nothing.** `HttpClient::set_accept_language` is `pub`, and `accept_language_override_reaches_the_wire` proves it reaches the socket — but nothing in the tree calls it outside that test.

**4. `navigator.language` has no override hook**, unlike its neighbours:

```js
defGetter('userAgent',  function() { return globalThis.__obscura_ua || "…"; });
defGetter('platform',   function() { return globalThis.__obscura_platform || "Win32"; });
defGetter('language',   function() { return "en-US"; });
defGetter('languages',  function() { return ["en-US", "en"]; });
```

So a client that asks for `de-DE` is told the call succeeded and gets `en-US` on every surface — a wrong answer rather than a missing one. That is the same shape as #734, which was just fixed: there `Intl` disagreed with `navigator.language`; here the operator's stated locale disagrees with all four.

### Impact and workaround

Playwright's `newContext({ locale })` and `newContext({ userAgent })` both go through `Emulation.setUserAgentOverride`, so on obscura they are accepted and ignored. There is no workaround through CDP; `Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders` can force the header, but `navigator.language` stays `en-US` and then contradicts it.

### Notes

- I have a fix and will open a PR against this issue.
- Scoped deliberately to the locale half. `platform` is the same silent drop but lands in #481's territory, and `Intl`'s default locale cannot follow a mid-session override at all: V8 resolves the ICU default once per isolate and caches it at first `Intl` use, so a pin after isolate creation is a no-op. I verified that separately while checking #734 — moving `set_default_locale` below `JsRuntime::new` fails `intl_locale_matches_navigator_language_regardless_of_host`.

items.body:
### obscura version or commit

Source build at `9326880` (`main`), `--features render`. Compared against Chromium 147 over CDP.

### Affected area

CSSOM / `getComputedStyle`

### Summary

Auditing ~90 computed properties on a real page turned up **41 that return the empty string** and a handful that return a **wrong value**. An empty string is indistinguishable from "not set" to a caller, so code that branches on these silently takes the wrong path instead of failing visibly.

This is the same shape as #762 (which adds five of them); filing the rest together rather than piecemeal, since a table-driven default set would cover most of it in one go.

### Properties returning `''`

Chromium's value for each is given, taken from a plain `<div>` with nothing set:

```
background-image     none        background-size      auto        background-position  0% 0%
background-repeat    repeat      font-style           normal      word-spacing         0px
text-decoration      none        text-decoration-line none        text-indent          0px
list-style-position  outside     border-spacing       0px         caption-side         top
align-self           auto        flex-grow            0           flex-shrink          1
flex-basis           auto        grid-column          auto        grid-row             auto
transition-property  all         transition-duration  0s          animation-name       none
animation-duration   0s          animation-iteration-count 1      animation-timing-function ease
user-select          auto        box-shadow           none        text-shadow          none
content              normal      order                0           object-fit           fill
resize               none        appearance           none        filter               none
mix-blend-mode       normal      writing-mode         horizontal-tb   direction        ltr
unicode-bidi         isolate     isolation            auto        contain              none
aspect-ratio         auto        zoom                 1
```

`animation-name` is worth calling out: it returns `''` even for an element with a **running** animation, where Chromium returns the animation's name.

### Properties returning a wrong value

Verified on minimal standalone fixtures, not just the real page:

| property | element | Chromium 147 | obscura |
|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | `<table>` | `table` | `block` |
| `flex-direction` | `<table>` | `row` | **`column`** |
| `align-items` | `<table>` | `normal` | **`stretch`** |
| `min-height` | plain `<div>` | `0px` | `auto` |
| `transition-property` | plain `<div>` | `all` | `none` |
| `outline-width` | plain `<div>` | `3px` (`medium`) | `0px` |

The first three look like the internal flex-based table model leaking into CSSOM: on a plain `<div>` both engines agree that `flex-direction` is `row` and `align-items` is `normal`, and it is only on a `<table>` that obscura reports `column` / `stretch`. Combined with `display` never returning `table` / `table-row` / `table-cell` / `list-item`, a table's box type cannot be read back at all, so layout has to be inferred from rects.

### How I found it

Diffing a Bootstrap admin against Chromium over CDP with a DOM-path-keyed probe. Happy to supply the audit script.

Two related items I have already sent PRs for, mentioned so this issue is not double-counted: #762 adds `vertical-align`, `list-style-type`, `border-collapse`, `table-layout`, `text-transform` and the `cssFloat` alias; #770 fixes `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left`, which were being served from `getBoundingClientRect` as viewport coordinates.

items.title: Default (non-stealth) client can't reach servers that only offer legacy TLS 1.2 CBC cipher suites — rustls-tls has no CBC support
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability (those go through SECURITY.md, not a public issue).

### obscura version or commit

0.1.11 (official binary)

### OS and architecture

Linux x86_64 (Debian 12, kernel 6.12.57)

### How are you using obscura?

CLI (fetch / serve / scrape / mcp)

### Affected area

Networking, cookies, or proxies

### Build variant

No-render with stealth (official no-render-stealth archive or --features stealth)

### Stealth mode

Off

### Reproduction

```
obscura fetch https://cgv.vn
```

### Expected behavior

The TLS handshake completes and the request succeeds, the same way `curl https://cgv.vn` and a `lightpanda fetch https://cgv.vn` both succeed from the identical host/IP (so this isn't an IP-reputation/anti-bot block).


### Actual behavior

The default client fails before any HTTP happens:
```
Error: Failed to navigate to https://cgv.vn: Network error: Network error: https://cgv.vn/: error sending request for url (https://cgv.vn/)
```
`RUST_LOG=trace` shows the TCP connection succeeds but nothing progresses past that — no TLS handshake debug output at all, consistent with rustls rejecting the handshake outright rather than a network-level failure.

Root cause: `cgv.vn`'s TLS edge only accepts legacy TLS 1.2 with CBC-mode cipher suites (no ALPN, no HTTP/2). It rejects every modern AEAD suite and TLS 1.3 outright:
```
$ echo | openssl s_client -connect cgv.vn:443 -tls1_3 -servername cgv.vn
...sslv3 alert handshake failure...

$ echo | openssl s_client -connect cgv.vn:443 -tls1_2 \
    -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305' -servername cgv.vn
...sslv3 alert handshake failure...

$ curl -v https://cgv.vn/ 2>&1 | grep -i "SSL connection"
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / AES128-SHA
```
`AES128-SHA` is a CBC-mode suite. `rustls` deliberately implements only modern AEAD cipher suites (no CBC), so `reqwest`'s `rustls-tls` backend (used by the default client since #229) can never complete a handshake with this class of server, regardless of what `--ca-cert`/`--insecure-disable-tls-host-verification` settings are passed.

Passing `--stealth` works around it, because that path uses `wreq` (BoringSSL), which — like curl and like `lightpanda`'s curl+BoringSSL networking — still negotiates legacy CBC suites fine. But `--stealth` shouldn't be a prerequisite for basic TLS compatibility with an otherwise-ordinary (if outdated) TLS server.

### Rendering details

_No response_

### Does headless Chrome behave the same?

I did not check. However: `curl` (OpenSSL) and `lightpanda fetch` (curl+BoringSSL) both succeed from the same machine/IP against the same URL.

### Logs

```shell
$ RUST_LOG=trace obscura fetch https://cgv.vn --dump html -v
DEBUG obscura: V8 flags: ...
Fetching https://cgv.vn...
DEBUG obscura_net::client: Cookie header for cgv.vn: 0 cookies (0 bytes)
TRACE hyper_util::client::legacy::pool: checkout waiting for idle connection: ("https", cgv.vn)
DEBUG reqwest::connect: starting new connection: https://cgv.vn/
TRACE hyper_util::client::legacy::connect::http: Http::connect; scheme=Some("https"), host=Some("cgv.vn"), port=None
DEBUG hyper_util::client::legacy::connect::http: connecting to 183.91.22.138:443
DEBUG hyper_util::client::legacy::connect::http: connected to 183.91.22.138:443
TRACE hyper_util::client::legacy::pool: checkout dropped for ("https", cgv.vn)
TRACE reqwest::retry: shouldn't retry!
Error: Failed to navigate to https://cgv.vn: Network error: Network error: https://cgv.vn/: error sending request for url (https://cgv.vn/)
```

items.title: width:calc(100% - 32px) resolves to 0 inside a flex subtree
items.body:
### obscura version or commit Source build at `9326880` (`main`), `--features render`. ### Affected area Layout / CSS ### Reproduction ```html
``` `getComputedStyle(document.getElementById('t')).width` ### Expected / actual | outer element | Chromium 147 | obscura | |---|---|---| | `display:flex;flex:1;width:1560px` | `142px` | **`0px`** | | `width:1560px` (no flex) | `1528px` | `1528px` | Without the flex ancestor both engines agree exactly. Add it and the `calc()` collapses to zero, so the control renders as a ~30px stub. ### What I think is happening `defer_cyclic_flex_inline_sizes` treats the size as cyclic because the *flex item* between the input and the flex container has an indefinite inline size. Two things then go wrong: 1. **An already-resolved value is discarded.** Instrumenting the neutralization shows the width is `Px(1528.0)` when the deferral runs — the expression had already been resolved against the containing block. It is replaced by the expression evaluated at a **zero** basis, which for `calc(100% - 32px)` clamps to `0px`. 2. **The basis re-sampled afterwards is the neutralized box's own padding.** `resolve_deferred_flex_inline_sizes` samples `content_box_width()` from the nearest rendered ancestor. Because every ancestor here is auto-width, they have all shrink-wrapped around the `0px` child, so the sampled basis comes back as **32.0** — which is the input's own `padding-left:25px` plus borders, not a containing block. `calc(32 - 32)` is then `0`. So the value ends up zero twice over, and the second pass cannot recover because the geometry it samples was produced by the first. For what it is worth, the `max_width` arm of that same match already avoids this by neutralizing to `Dimension::Auto` with the comment *"a cyclic percentage max-size behaves as its initial value during intrinsic contribution sizing"*. I tried the same for the `width` arm and it did not move the sampled basis (still 32), so the ancestors are evidently measured before that change takes effect — I did not want to guess further inside that pass. ### Why it matters in practice This is the Bootstrap/DataTables search field: `.data-table-search{width:calc(100% - 32px)}` inside `.dataTables_filter > label > span.input-icon`, under Preside's `.page-content-inner{display:flex}`. Every admin listing's search box renders as a ~34px stub with its placeholder text spilling outside it. I reduced a real admin page from 7,730 CSS rules to the three that matter (`.input-icon{position:relative}`, the `.data-table-search` rule, and `.page-content-inner{display:flex;flex:1}`) by delta debugging, which is what identified the flex ancestor as the trigger.

CMS
A much longer hidden string
``` `document.getElementById('t').getBoundingClientRect().width` ### Expected behavior `71.1` (Chromium 147). The second child is `display:none`, so it generates no box and cannot contribute to the parent float's shrink-to-fit width. ### Actual behavior `82` — the hidden element's content width leaks into the parent. ### The trigger is the combination, not either half | case | Chromium 147 | obscura | |---|---|---| | atomic inline + `display:none` float | 71.1 | **82** | | atomic inline, no hidden float | 71.1 | 71 | | `display:none` float, no atomic inline | 31.1 | 32 | | `display:none` **without** `float` + atomic inline | 71.1 | 71 | So the hidden element is correctly ignored on its own, and the inline-blocks are sized correctly on their own. 1
2
3
4
``` Measure each column's width and its parent `.row`'s height at a 1700px viewport. ### Expected behavior All four are 1333px (83.333% of 1600), and every `.row` has non-zero height. Chrome 147: ``` 1 float+pct w=1333 x=10 rowH=18 2 float+pct+PCTmargin w=1333 x=143 rowH=18 3 float+pct+pxmargin w=1333 x=143 rowH=18 4 pct+PCTmargin w=1333 x=143 rowH=18 ``` ### Actual behavior ``` 1 float+pct w=1333 x=10 rowH=19 ok 2 float+pct+PCTmargin w=420 x=143 rowH=0 <-- wrong width AND parent collapses 3 float+pct+pxmargin w=873 x=696 rowH=19 <-- wrong width 4 pct+PCTmargin w=1334 x=143 rowH=19 ok ``` A float with a percentage width is correct **until it also has a margin**. Then it collapses towards its content width (`420` is roughly the 370px child plus padding). With a percentage margin the parent's clearfix also stops working and `.row` reports height 0, so following in-flow content is laid out over the float instead of below it. Float alone is fine. Percentage margin alone is fine. It is the combination. ### Impact This is the Bootstrap 3 grid. `.col-*-N` is `float:left; width:N/12%` and `.col-*-offset-M` adds `margin-left:M/12%`, so any offset column mis-sizes and its row collapses. Measured on a real Bootstrap 3 admin at a 1600px viewport, walking up from a form field — every ancestor agrees until the grid column: ``` Chrome obscura DIV.row w=1600 w=1600 agree DIV.col-sm-10.col-sm-offset-1 w=1333 w=445 <-- diverges here DIV.login-container w=370 w=370 ``` Everything below inherits the error: the page's centred panel lands at x=190 instead of x=635, `document.body` measures 450px tall instead of 806, and a block that should follow the row is painted over the form — `elementFromPoint` at the form field returns that block rather than the input, so coordinate-based clicks land on the wrong element. Data tables on the same pages show the related symptom: the `` is the full 1518px but its columns only occupy 821px, leaving a third of the table empty, where Chrome distributes all 1518px. ### Does headless Chrome behave the same? No — Chrome 147 output above, all four correct. ### Note This looks like the same family as #749 (functional `flex-basis` evaluated without a containing block, so the item fell back to content width): a definite length not resolved against the containing block, and the element shrink-fits instead.

The breakpoint is where Vector 2022 switches to its three-column layout. ### Where it goes wrong The paragraph itself is laid out correctly for the space it is given. At a 1280px viewport: | element | width | |---|---| | `section` containing the article body | 752px | | lead `

` | 97px | | `.infobox` (floated right) | 641px | 752 - 641 = 111, so the paragraph gets what is left beside the float. The infobox is the problem, not the paragraph. The governing rule is @media (min-width:640px){ .mw-parser-output .infobox { margin-left:1em; float:right; clear:right; width:22em } } 22em at a 16px root is 352px. We lay it out at 641px. ### The part I find most suspicious In situ, that width cannot be overridden at all: ib.style.width = '22em' -> still 641 -> still 641 But the element is perfectly capable of being narrow. Cloning it into a plain 752px `

`: | clone | width | |---|---| | classes stripped, `style="width:22em"` | **352** (correct) | | classes stripped, `style="float:right;width:22em"` | 352 | | classes stripped, `style="max-width:22em"` | 352 | | classes stripped, no width | 491 | | **classes kept**, `style="width:22em"` | **310** | and a `width:0` probe on the original gives 310. So the used width in its real position (641) is neither the specified width, nor min-content, nor what the same subtree produces elsewhere. ### What I ruled out Each of these behaves correctly in an isolated fixture, so none of them is the cause on its own: - `em` widths inside `@media (min-width:...)`, with and without a space after `@media` - descendant selectors inside `@media` - `@media all and (max-width:calc(640px - 1px))` — Wikipedia ships this; a following rule still applies - a table honouring a specified width, and its cell text wrapping to it - `float:right` combined with a specified width - `!important` beating an earlier rule, on both a table and a div I could not reduce it to a minimal fixture; every reduction I built rendered correctly. It seems to need the real cascade, which is why I am reporting it against the URL rather than as a `render-repros` case. Happy to keep bisecting if you can point me at where a specified width would be discarded during table layout.

items.title: HTMLElement.click() does not honor the click in progress flag
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. (The closed stack-overflow issues are deep-DOM recursive traversal; this is re-entrant event dispatch.)
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability.

### obscura version or commit

v0.2.1 release binary and a source build at `f449e6fb3183138eb3e80f11fe44af31cefe0fae` (`main`)

### OS and architecture

Linux x86_64

### How are you using obscura?

CLI (fetch / serve / scrape / mcp)

### Affected area

JavaScript or DOM behavior

### Build variant

Render-enabled (--features render)

### Stealth mode

Off

### Reproduction

```
obscura fetch 'data:text/html,<button id=x>b</button>' --eval "(function(){ var n=0; var x=document.getElementById('x'); x.onclick=function(){ n++; if(n<5000) x.click(); }; x.click(); return n; })()"
```

`5000` is above the stack limit observed here, so the repro still reaches the swallowed `RangeError`, and it also caps execution on a build with a larger stack. Without the guard, recursion continues until stack exhaustion.

### Expected behavior

`1`. Per HTML, `click()` first returns for a disabled form control, then returns if the element's click in progress flag is set. Otherwise it sets the flag, fires a synthetic pointer event named `click`, and unsets the flag, so a handler that clicks its own element cannot re-enter. Headless Chrome returns `1`.

### Actual behavior

The command returned `2017` on this host on both v0.2.1 and `main`. The depth is stack-size dependent; without the guard, dispatch continues until stack exhaustion.

`click()` has no click in progress flag, so each dispatch re-enters until the stack runs out. The resulting `RangeError` is raised inside the listener, and `dispatchEvent` wraps every listener in `try { ... } catch(e) { console.error(e) }` (`bootstrap.js`, the inline-handler and registered-handler loops), so it is logged to stderr and does not propagate. The caller sees `click()` return normally: a `try`/`catch` around the outer `click()` catches nothing, and no `error` event or `window.onerror` fires. So one `click()` recurses to stack exhaustion, and the overflow surfaces only as a console trace.

### Does headless Chrome behave the same?

No. Chrome dispatches once.

### Additional context

Proposed fix and regression test: https://github.com/Vrejf/obscura/commit/495fadb

A `WeakSet` of elements with a click in progress, checked and set around the dispatch in `try`/`finally`. Behaviour verified against headless Chrome on the cases the guard could plausibly break:

| case | Chrome | stock | fixed |
|---|---|---|---|
| handler clicks its own element | 1 | to stack exhaustion | 1 |
| three sequential clicks | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| flag clears after a listener throws | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| handler clicks a different element | fires both | fires both | fires both |
| mutual recursion, A clicks B clicks A | 2 | to stack exhaustion | 2 |

Also `cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast` at 1493/1493. The obstacle course scores 32/33 on both the base and fixed commits, failing `observer-intersection` identically (`expected 'io:50', got ''`), so it is unrelated to this change.

The branch also carries fixes for #721 and #722. This commit touches only `bootstrap.js` and its test, so it is independent of both.

items.title: getBoundingClientRect returns 0x0 for inline elements in a run that cannot fold (replaced, inline-block, block, float or out-of-flow sibling)
items.body:
### Before you start - [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. - [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`. - [x] This is not a security vulnerability. ### obscura version or commit v0.2.1 release binary and a source build at `f449e6fb3183138eb3e80f11fe44af31cefe0fae` (`main`) ### OS and architecture Linux x86_64 ### How are you using obscura? CDP server with Puppeteer or Playwright (also reproduces via CLI `--eval`) ### Affected area JavaScript or DOM behavior ### Build variant Render-enabled (--features render) ### Stealth mode Off ### Reproduction ``` obscura fetch 'data:text/html,
' --eval "(function(){ var r = document.getElementById('l').getBoundingClientRect(); return r.width + 'x' + r.height; })()" ``` The trigger is the sibling, not the element: `
` measures correctly. Any atomic inline in the same run reproduces it (`input`, `button`, `img`, `textarea`, a text sibling plus an input, `span` instead of `label`); all verified 0x0 against Chrome on a 10-case matrix. ### Expected behavior About `48x17` (headless Chrome 145). The label should be a coordinate-click hit target. ### Actual behavior `0x0`, so Puppeteer/Playwright `handle.click()` fails with "not clickable". Root cause as far as I can tell: a run containing a replaced element fails `try_build_run` and takes the mixed-run path in `build_mixed_block`, where `is_flattenable_inline` splices the wrapper's children directly into the parent's Taffy children. The wrapper never gets a layout box, so nothing records a rect for it; `synthesize_ordinary_inline_fragments` skips it because it requires an existing `rects` entry. ~~Painting is unaffected; this is DOM geometry only.~~ **Correction:** that is wrong. Flattening also drops the wrapper's own horizontal margin and padding from layout, so the following content is painted in the wrong place. The trigger set is also wider than a replaced sibling, and there is a second code path with the same symptom. See the follow-up comment below for the measurements: https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura/issues/722#issuecomment-5601628752 Combined with #721 this makes the common `` checkbox pattern fully inoperable: the label has no activation behaviour and no hit-target either. ### Does headless Chrome behave the same? No. Chrome reports the real fragment geometry. ### Additional context I have a fix that synthesizes the flattened wrapper's rect after layout as the union of its rendered descendants' element rects and per-word text runs, excluding positioned inlines (a positioned inline is a containing block for absolute descendants; installing a rect changes how those resolve, and broke `positioned_counter_inside_nested_inline_code_uses_the_code_gutter` until excluded): https://github.com/Vrejf/obscura/commit/8285e0b The same pass has to avoid three traps, all verified against Chrome: an out-of-flow descendant must not stretch the union (a `position:absolute` child at `left:900px` otherwise turns a 28px span into a 918px one), fragments must be merged per line rather than per word or `getClientRects()` returns one rect per word, and a padded inline should keep a real box instead of being flattened at all (`is_flattenable_inline` excludes borders and backgrounds today but not padding). The descendant walk is depth-capped, matching the `descendants()` guard in `tree.rs`. Verification: the geometry matrices match Chrome within font-metric noise; `cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast` 1493/1493; the no-render build and its tests (449/449); obstacle course unchanged at 32/33 with the one failure also failing on stock; all 69 `render-repros` fixtures produce metrics byte-identical to the pre-change build, so nothing repaints differently; interleaved perf runs show no regression (58 vs 55 ms median on a fixture, 1358 vs 1351 ms on a synthetic page with 3000 flattened wrappers). Known residuals I left alone rather than install guessed geometry: an empty inline reports `0x0` where Chrome reports `0x`, and an inline wrapping only a replaced element gets the replaced element's height rather than the line box's (`8x8` vs Chrome's `8x16`). Both need the inline strut, which the existing `synthesize_ordinary_inline_fragments` path derives from the text engine. Happy to open a PR.

items.title: Binary fetch and interception bodies are corrupted by UTF-8 conversion
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability.

### obscura version or commit

`f449e6fb3183138eb3e80f11fe44af31cefe0fae` (`main`)

### OS and architecture

macOS arm64

### How are you using obscura?

Embedded Rust library and CDP server.

### Affected area

JavaScript fetch/XHR, networking, and CDP request interception.

### Build variant

Render-enabled. The stealth transport is affected by the same string conversion.

### Stealth mode

Both off and on.

### Reproduction

Send a request body containing bytes that are not valid UTF-8:

```js
fetch(url, {
  method: "POST",
  body: new Uint8Array([0, 128, 255, 16]),
});
```

The same problem is observable with `Blob`, `ArrayBuffer`, sliced typed-array views, binary `File` values in `FormData`, and `XMLHttpRequest.send()`.

For the CDP fulfill path, resolve an intercepted request with:

```json
{
  "method": "Fetch.fulfillRequest",
  "params": {
    "responseCode": 200,
    "body": "AP+Awyg="
  }
}
```

`AP+Awyg=` represents the bytes `[0, 255, 128, 195, 40]`.

### Expected behavior

Request and fulfilled response bodies remain byte-for-byte identical across the JavaScript, Rust transport, public interception API, and CDP boundaries.

### Actual behavior

Binary request bodies pass through JavaScript/Rust strings and are UTF-8 encoded. For example, `[0, 128, 255, 16]` reaches the server as `[0, 194, 128, 195, 191, 16]`. A `Request` object's inherited body is also dropped when `fetch(request)` has no explicit `init.body`.

The CDP fulfill bridge decodes base64 and then uses lossy UTF-8 conversion, replacing non-UTF-8 bytes. CDP `continueRequest.postData` is also modeled as a string instead of raw bytes.

### Does headless Chrome behave the same?

No. Chrome preserves the original request and fulfilled response bytes.

### Proposed split

1. Preserve binary JavaScript fetch/XHR bodies through the normal and stealth transports without changing the public interception API.
2. Change interception request/response bodies to `Vec<u8>` and decode CDP base64 directly into bytes.

items.title: Feature: persistent profile / user-data-dir for fetch & scrape (storage is lost between CLI invocations)
items.body:
### Version / platform
- obscura 0.2.0 (official aarch64-linux release binary), Ubuntu proot on Termux

### Problem
Every `obscura fetch` invocation runs in a fresh context: localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies and IndexedDB do not survive between runs.

```bash
obscura fetch URL --eval "localStorage.setItem('k','v');'set'"      # → 'set'
obscura fetch URL --eval "localStorage.getItem('k')||'GONE'"        # → 'GONE'
```

This makes multi-step E2E flows impossible with the CLI alone — e.g. "log in on /auth, then verify an authenticated page renders" needs one persistent browser context across navigations. The only current workaround is `obscura serve` + a CDP client, which defeats the point of the simple CLI for local-app testing (we hit this testing a localhost PWA's login flow).

### Request
One of:
- `--user-data-dir <dir>` (and/or `--profile <name>`) for `fetch`/`scrape` that persists storage to disk and reuses it across invocations
- or an `--keep-alive` mode where one process serves sequential `fetch` calls against the same context
- or at minimum a docs section describing the recommended CDP pattern for multi-step flows

Related but distinct: #678 (sessionStorage not surviving navigation *within* one run) — this issue is about persistence *across* processes.

### Environment details
- Obscura version: 0.2.0 (release binary)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (proot) on Android/Termux aarch64

items.title: `browser_navigate` never returns on ad-heavy pages — renderer spins at ~100% CPU indefinitely (v0.2.0)
items.body:
## Summary

`browser_navigate` (MCP server) hangs forever on pages with heavy consent-manager/ad-stack JavaScript. The obscura process enters a ~100% CPU spin (state R, 16 threads) and the JSON-RPC request never returns — no timeout, no error. The call stays pending indefinitely, which stalls any agent/automation loop waiting on it. Killing the process is the only recovery.

## Environment

- obscura 0.2.0 (release build, x86_64-linux, binary dated 2026-08-08)
- Command: `obscura mcp --stealth --allow-private-network` (reproduced with plain `obscura mcp` as well)
- Linux (Docker container, Debian-based), MCP over stdio
- Client: custom JSON-RPC stdio client (initialize → tools/call browser_navigate)

## Steps to reproduce

Minimal Python client that hangs deterministically:

```python
import subprocess, json, sys, select, time

URL = "https://www.wftv.com/news/local/daytona-beach-officer-joel-llinas-fired-after-viral-handcuffing-video/HAPIMHP5BVAWDNTMJ4CMI2XUOY/?utm_term=Autofeed&utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Facebook#Echobox=1787068907"

p = subprocess.Popen(["obscura", "mcp"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                     stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)

def send(obj):
    p.stdin.write(json.dumps(obj) + "\n"); p.stdin.flush()

def recv(timeout):
    r, _, _ = select.select([p.stdout], [], [], timeout)
    return json.loads(p.stdout.readline()) if r else None

send({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{
    "protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},
    "clientInfo":{"name":"repro","version":"1.0"}}})
recv(30)
send({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"})

t0 = time.time()
send({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{
    "name":"browser_navigate","arguments":{"url": URL}}})
r = recv(75)   # returns None — request never completes
print(f"elapsed {time.time()-t0:.0f}s, response: {r}")
```

## Observed behavior

- `browser_navigate` does not return within 75s in a clean test; in production it burned 27+ minutes until manually killed
- Process stats during hang: `%CPU ~98`, state `R`, `NLWP 16`, `TIME` accumulating continuously
- Deterministic: same result on every attempt (reproduced twice in production on the same URL by an automation agent, once in a clean isolated instance)
- stderr shows a burst of script errors from the page's consent/ads stack, then silence:

```
WARN obscura_browser::page: Failed to fetch script https://shorts.wftv.com/vs.js?cid=8CU812SX1: Network error
WARN obscura_browser::page: Script error (https://cmp.osano.com/.../osano.js): JS error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')
WARN obscura_browser::page: Inline script error: JS error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'close')
WARN obscura_browser::page: Inline script error: JS error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'optOut')
WARN obscura_browser::page: Script error (https://d3plfjw9uod7ab.cloudfront.net/....js): JS error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')
```

Scripts involved on this page: Osano CMP (cmp.osano.com), a CloudFront-delivered bundle, rubicon, amazon-aax, ntv.io, googletagservices.

## Expected behavior

- `browser_navigate` should return (success or error) within the operation timeout
- A page whose JS misbehaves should never wedge the navigation promise or pin a CPU core indefinitely

## Notes

- The V8 watchdog appears to terminate *synchronous* script overruns, but this looks like a spinning async task / event loop livelock inside a renderer isolate that no operation-level timeout covers
- Related: any background tab running adversarial or busy-loop JS also spins indefinitely after the operation "completes" — closing the tab kills the isolate. A per-tab idle/activity watchdog would cover both cases
- Workaround we use: external watchdog that SIGKILLs obscura when a request stays in-flight >3 min, then respawns

## Impact

Any MCP client (or agent) calling `browser_navigate` on a mainstream news/ads page gets permanently stuck. This makes obscura unusable unattended on a large fraction of real-world sites.

items.title: Runtime.evaluate returns 'No page' on freshly created tab via CDP
items.body:
## Description

`Runtime.evaluate` returns `{"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"No page"}}` on a freshly created tab, even after `Page.navigate` and `Runtime.enable` both succeed. This prevents any JS execution (DOM reads, injections, event dispatch) via the CDP websocket connection.

## Reproduction

1. Start obscura: `./obscura serve -p 9333`
2. Open a page via CDP:
   ```python
   tabs = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:9333/json", timeout=5))
   page = next(t for t in tabs if t.get("type")=="page")
   ws = await websockets.connect(page["webSocketDebuggerUrl"])
   ```
3. Enable domains + navigate:
   ```python
   await ws.send(json.dumps({"id":1,"method":"Runtime.enable","params":{}}))
   await ws.send(json.dumps({"id":2,"method":"Page.navigate","params":{"url":"https://example.com"}}))
   await asyncio.sleep(3)
   ```
4. Evaluate — fails:
   ```python
   await ws.send(json.dumps({"id":3,"method":"Runtime.evaluate",
       "params":{"expression":"1+1","returnByValue":True}}))
   # Returns: {'id': 3, 'error': {'code': -32601, 'message': 'No page'}}
   ```

## Expected behavior

`Runtime.evaluate` returns the result of the expression (e.g. `{"result":{"type":"number","value":2}}`) — same as Chrome DevTools Protocol.

## Actual behavior

`Runtime.evaluate` returns `{"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"No page"}}` regardless of the expression.

## Environment

- obscura v0.2.0 (`obscura-aarch64-macos-stealth.tar.gz`)
- macOS 15.7 (Intel x86_64)
- Also reproduced on: `obscura-x86_64-macos-stealth` (same error)

## Notes

- `Page.navigate` dispatches successfully (response id comes back with no error)
- `Page.enable`, `Runtime.enable` both return `{}` (success)
- The websocket connection itself is stable (events like `Page.loadEventFired` fire)
- This appears to be a page-attachment issue: the page object exists (visible in `/json` endpoint, has a URL), but `Runtime.evaluate` can't find it

## CDP endpoints observed

- `/json` → returns the tab list with valid `webSocketDebuggerUrl`
- `ws://127.0.0.1:9333/devtools/page/page-1` → accepts commands, returns responses
- `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` works fine (response id matches)
- Only `Runtime.evaluate` fails with "No page"

items.title: prepare_screenshot_resources fetches CSS resources from the stylesheet text instead of the render tree
items.body:
## The Problem

`prepare_screenshot_resources` (`crates/obscura-browser/src/page.rs:2772`) collects the resources to load with `css_resource_urls(&css, &base_url)` (`page.rs:2824`). The source is the **text** of the stylesheet, not the render tree. A rule that matches no element on the page is fetched anyway.

For a complete screenshot this is understandable. But it has an effect that goes beyond rendering: where such an address changes server state, the fetch destroys it.

This is not a spec violation. CSS Images 3 and CSS Values 4 do not prescribe the timing of a load. The argument is the consistent behavior of two engines, and the effect.

## Measured

Login page of an SAP AppRouter, reachable without logging in, so reproducible without access: `https://sappubliccatalog.authentication.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/login`

| | protected background images | font-awesome fonts | total fonts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chromium 151 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| Firefox 150 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| obscura | 4 | 6 | 18 |

The four images are in `application.css` and match no rendered element:

```
url('/images/gray-cloud.png')   url('/images/logo-pcf.png')
url('/images/logo-pws.png')     url('/images/p-logo.png')
```

All four respond with `302` to `/login`. Cross-checked with curl.

## Why this is more than unnecessary traffic

Every call to `/login` mints a new OAuth `state` into the session and delivers it in the page. The four image requests go via `302` to `/login` and thereby overwrite the `state` the page has just received. The callback fails with `state_not_verified`, the round starts over, and obscura aborts with `Too many redirects`.

Fetching a resource nobody displays therefore makes the login impossible.

## Reproduction without SAP

Four endpoints are enough. The page carries a stylesheet with a rule that no element uses, and whose `background-image` points to a protected address.

```
/login             mints a new state on EVERY GET, serves HTML with
                   <link rel="stylesheet"> and the link to /authorize?state=...
/style.css         .not-used-by-any-element { background-image: url('/protected/bg.png'); }
/protected/bg.png  302 to /login
/callback          compares the state with the most recently minted one
```

**Expected:** one `/login`, zero image fetches, the callback succeeds.
**Observed with obscura:** 20 logins, 10 image fetches, `state_not_verified`.

Chromium and Firefox report `LOGIN OK`.

## Two things that are relevant

**The env switches are no substitute for a fix.** Three call sites each have their own switch (`page.rs:2298`, `2629`, `2652`). Setting all three to `0` fixes the loop. But measured on a page without a redirect, this also costs the **used** background images:

| | unused image | used image |
|---|---|---|
| Chromium 151 | 0 | 1 |
| obscura, default | 1 | 1 |
| obscura, switches off | 0 | 0 |

Screenshots lose all CSS backgrounds this way. The switch is therefore not suitable as a general recommendation.

**The function has a legitimate purpose.** A screenshot should be complete, and binding to the render tree is more costly than reading the stylesheet text. This is a trade-off, not an oversight. That is why this is an issue and not a pull request: the decision belongs to the maintainers.

For comparison, the structure in Gecko. `StartImageLoads` is attached there to `ComputedStyle`, that is, to the computed style of an element, not to the stylesheet. The comment in the source code says "Start image loads for this style." (`layout/style/ComputedStyle.h`).

items.title: Fetch interception blocks every matched subresource outright instead of pausing and asking the client
items.body: ### Summary When a CDP client enables Fetch interception, obscura treats the interception patterns as a block list for static subresources: any ` ``` Connect with puppeteer, `page.setRequestInterception(true)`, abort requests matching `*.css*`, continue the rest, navigate. Expected (Chrome): `marker-dep-ran`, stylesheet aborted. Actual: `marker-dep-missing` — `dep.js` was blocked engine-side and the interception handler never saw either request. The engine logs `Blocked script by interception: .../dep.js`. ### Proposed fix - `should_block_url` consults only `Network.setBlockedURLs` patterns. - Static subresource fetches (scripts, stylesheets, stylesheet `@import`s) that match active interception patterns are paused on the existing `InterceptedRequest` channel and the client's verdict is obeyed: Continue (with URL override), Fail (skip the resource), Fulfill (use the provided response). Fail-open on a closed channel or an unresponsive client so a crashed client cannot stall rendering. PR incoming with an end-to-end regression test.

items.title: getComputedStyle() methods throw "this._owner.getAttribute is not a function" on every element (breaks jQuery .css()/.show())
items.body:
### Summary On v0.1.11, calling any CSSOM method on the object returned by `getComputedStyle(el)` throws `TypeError: this._owner.getAttribute is not a function`, for every element whose style declaration has an owner (i.e. all elements). Property access works (`cs.color` returns the right value); method calls (`cs.getPropertyValue('color')`, `cs.item(0)`, reading `cs.cssText` or `cs.length`) throw. jQuery's `curCSS` reads `computed.getPropertyValue(name)`, so every jQuery `.css()` read and `.show()` fails. Found in the wild on https://www.dasa-raegister.com/formazione/iso-9001/ where the throw aborts WooCommerce's `wc_variation_form` init, so the selected variation's price never reaches the DOM and the rendered HTML loses content that a real browser shows on load. ### Reproduction ```html
box
``` Also observable through the same proxy: `'_loaded' in cs` is `false` and `cs._loaded` / `cs._owner` read as `""` instead of the declaration's own fields. ### Root cause Two proxy layers in `crates/obscura-js/js/bootstrap.js` interact badly: 1. The `getComputedStyle` wrapper proxies the element's live style proxy and its `get` trap does `if (prop in target) return target[prop]`, handing methods back unbound. `computed.getPropertyValue(name)` therefore runs with `this` bound to the outer proxy, not the declaration. This also makes the trap's own `getPropertyValue`/`item`/`length`/`cssText` fallbacks dead code, since those names are always `in` the target's prototype. 2. `_styleProxy`'s `has` trap never consults the target's own properties for string keys (only the prototype, parsed props, and the CSS name set), so the declaration's own fields `_loaded`, `_props`, `_owner` report absent through the outer proxy and fall through to its CSS-name lookup, which returns `""`. 3. Inside `_pull()`, `this._loaded` then reads `""` (falsy, so the guard does not bail) and `this._owner` reads `""`, and `"".getAttribute(...)` throws. Regression introduced with the owner-backed live declarations from the #488 fix; owner-less declarations never dereference `_owner` so the pre-#488 code was immune. ### Proposed fix In the `getComputedStyle` wrapper's `get` trap, serve the computed-style method fallbacks (`getPropertyValue` backed by the inline+defaults lookup, `item`, `length`, `cssText`, `getPropertyPriority`, `parentRule`) before the `prop in target` passthrough, and bind any function that does pass through to the target declaration. No change to `_styleProxy`'s `has` trap, so `'_loaded' in el.style` stays false like a real browser. PR incoming.

items.title: Request: support --storage-dir in `obscura mcp` for persistent cookies/session
items.body:
### Feature Description

The `obscura mcp` subcommand (both stdio and `--http` transports) does not support `--storage-dir`, so cookies/localStorage live only in process memory and are lost on restart. Please consider adding `--storage-dir` support to `obscura mcp` (or confirm whether it's planned).

### Motivation

MCP is the primary way agents (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, custom agent stacks) drive Obscura, and `obscura mcp --http` is the documented sidecar deployment pattern. In Docker/container deployments, persistent sessions matter:

1. `docker run` + `obscura mcp --http` with a mounted volume — users expect `--storage-dir` to work like it does for `serve`/`fetch` so a login survives container restarts.
2. The only current workaround is exporting/importing session state through the `browser_storage_state` / `browser_set_storage_state` MCP tools (agent-side JSON persistence), which works but is manual, fragile for large storage, and not what a volume mount implies.
3. `fetch`, `serve`, and `scrape` all accept `--storage-dir` (confirmed in `crates/obscura-cli/src/main.rs`); `obscura_mcp::run()` / `http::run()` simply don't receive the parameter today.

### Proposed Solution

Wire `--storage-dir` into the `mcp` subcommand and pass it through to the browser/cookie store, with the same semantics as `serve`: all sessions in the process read/write one directory (`cookies.json` + `localStorage/<origin>.json`), written on clean exit and after each navigation.

### Alternatives Considered

- Keeping agent-side `browser_storage_state` JSON round-trips (works, but manual and not volume-mount friendly).
- An env var (e.g. `OBSCURA_STORAGE_DIR`) as an alternative to the flag — either is fine; the flag would match the other subcommands.

items.title: `request.continue()` overrides are silently dropped for all intercepted requests
Target.getTargets returns empty for new connections — pages not globally visible (CDP spec violation)
items.body:
## Root cause found — regression from #456

Found the cause while reading the source. `Target.getTargets` itself is correct (iterates `ctx.pages`), but **`CdpContext.pages` is per-connection**. PR #456 (merged 2026-07-22) deliberately gave each WebSocket connection its own default browser context for cookie/UA isolation — and targets live in that per-connection context, so a new connection enumerates only its own (empty) pages.

That also explains why this wasn't reported earlier: it's a regression introduced ~1 week before the 0.1.11 build we tested.

## Suggested fix (Chrome semantics)

- Keep per-context data isolation (cookies/headers/UA) as #456 intended.
- Move the **target registry** to server-level shared state so `getTargets`/setDiscoverTargets see all live pages across connections, each tagged with its `browserContextId` (the code already carries `page.context.id`).
- Route page ops by sessionId → the owning context (already how the dispatcher routes by `{targetId}-session`).
- Serialize access through the existing global `v8_lock`.

This matches Chromium: targets are globally visible, but each belongs to a browser context; a client attaches and operates via sessionId.

items.title: [Feature] Configurable module evaluation timeout, DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded CDP support, and V8 watchdog tuning for complex SPA hydration
items.body:
## Summary

Thank you for Obscura — it's a great lightweight option for browser automation and E2E testing workflows. While integrating it with a Playwright-driven test suite against a modern TypeScript SPA (Astro 5 + Vue 3 + Vite dev server), I encountered a few issues that block broader adoption. Opening this as a consolidated feature/enhancement request.

## Environment

| Component         | Version                                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Obscura           | v0.1.9                                                 |
| Node.js           | 20.x                                                   |
| OS                | Ubuntu (Linux)                                         |
| Automation client | Playwright 1.52                                        |
| Target app        | TypeScript SPA with Astro 5 + Vue 3 islands + Vite HMR |

---

## Issue 1: Module evaluation timeout too short for Vite HMR client

**Observed behavior:**

```
Module evaluation timed out after 3000ms: http://localhost:4321/@vite/client
```

Vite's HMR client requires more than 3000 ms to evaluate during initial connection to the dev server. The hard timeout kills the module, which cascades into a broken dev server integration — the SPA never bootstraps correctly under Obscura.

**Expected behavior:**

The HMR client evaluates successfully and the SPA dev server works out of the box.

**Requested change:**

Make the module evaluation timeout configurable, e.g.:
- Environment variable: `OBSCURA_EVAL_TIMEOUT_MS=10000`
- Or CLI flag: `--eval-timeout=10000`
- Or a sensible default increase (e.g., 10 000 ms) with an override mechanism

---

## Issue 2: V8 watchdog terminates synchronous overrun during SPA hydration

**Observed behavior:**

```
V8 watchdog fired: terminated a synchronous overrun
```

This occurs during complex island hydration in a multi-component Vue 3 + Astro setup. The watchdog appears to use a threshold optimized for simpler pages, and fires prematurely on legitimate (though heavy) synchronous initialization work common in modern SPA frameworks.

**Requested change:**

- Expose a watchdog timeout configuration (env var / CLI flag), or
- Increase the default threshold to accommodate complex hydration workloads, or
- Provide a `--no-watchdog` escape hatch for testing scenarios

---

## Issue 3: Missing CDP method — `DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`

**Observed behavior:**

```
CDP error for DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded: Unknown DOM method
```

Playwright (and likely other CDP-based automation tools) call `DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` internally before performing click/fill actions on elements outside the current viewport. Since Obscura does not implement this method, those actions fail silently or throw.

**Requested change:**

Implement `DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` in the CDP server. If a full implementation is non-trivial, a no-op stub that returns success would unblock most automation workflows (since Obscura has no visual layout engine and scrolling is a no-op by nature).

---

## Issue 4: `Page.captureScreenshot` not supported (acknowledged)

```
Page.captureScreenshot is not supported by Obscura: no layout or paint engine
```

Noting this for completeness — understood that this is an expected architectural limitation. Visual regression testing is not possible, but functional/E2E testing is the primary use case here, so this is acceptable.

---

## Impact

These issues collectively prevent using Obscura as a drop-in lightweight browser for E2E test suites targeting modern TypeScript SPAs with Vite-based dev servers and component hydration. Issues 1–3 have clear, relatively contained fixes and would significantly improve the developer experience.

## Proposed Priority

1. **Issue 3** (`DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`) — blocks basic interaction with any element outside the viewport; a no-op stub would suffice
2. **Issue 1** (evaluation timeout) — simple configuration change, high impact for Vite users
3. **Issue 2** (V8 watchdog) — tuning/configuration, important for complex SPAs

---

## Additional Context

All logs were captured running `obscura serve --port 9222` with Playwright tests targeting an Astro 5 dev server. Happy to provide full log dumps, minimal reproductions, or help test fixes if needed.

Thanks for the project!

items.title: navigator.userAgent contradicts the User-Agent request header on every platform
items.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I tested against the latest release or `main`.
- [x] This is not a security vulnerability (those go through SECURITY.md, not a public issue).

### obscura version or commit

0.1.10 (official release binary) and e314b9b (built from source, 2026-07-24)

### OS and architecture

Windows 11 x86_64 and Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 (WSL2) — reproduced identically on both.

### How are you using obscura?

CLI (fetch / serve / scrape / mcp)

### Stealth mode

None

### Reproduction

# what the server receives
obscura fetch https://postman-echo.com/headers --dump original --stealth

# what the page sees
obscura fetch https://example.com --stealth \
  --eval 'navigator.userAgent + " || platform=" + navigator.platform'

### Expected behavior

The `User-Agent` request header, the `Sec-CH-UA-Platform` client hint and
`navigator.userAgent` / `navigator.platform` should tell the server one consistent story,
the way a real browser does by construction.

### Actual behavior


They disagree. `navigator.*` always reports **Windows**, regardless of the host platform,
while the request header always reports the **real** platform:

| | HTTP request header | JS on the page |
|---|---|---|
| **Linux host** | `Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) ... Chrome/145.0.0.0` | `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ... Chrome/145.0.0.0` |
| `Sec-CH-UA-Platform` | `"Linux"` | `navigator.platform` → `Win32` |
| **Windows host** | `Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) ... Chrome/145.0.0.0` | `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ... Chrome/145.0.0.0` |
| `Sec-CH-UA-Platform` | `"Linux"` | `navigator.platform` → `Win32` |

So on Linux the header is right and JS is wrong; on Windows *both* are wrong, in opposite
directions. Either way the two never match, and a one-line server-side check catches it.

**Additionally, without `--stealth` the Chrome version itself disagrees:**

```
header:              ... Chrome/145.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
navigator.userAgent: ... Chrome/143.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
```

With `--stealth` both report 145, so only the OS part remains mismatched in that mode.

**A possibly related signal:** obscura sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br`, whereas Chrome 145
sends `gzip, deflate, br, zstd`.

### Comparison with headless Chrome

Headless Chrome does not exhibit this: it derives the header and `navigator.userAgent` from
the same string, so they cannot drift apart.

### Stealth mode

Reproduces both with and without `--stealth`.

### Impact and workaround

Passing `--user-agent` explicitly fixes it — the flag correctly propagates to
`Sec-CH-UA-Platform` as well, and all four values line up.

The practical difference is large. On `rozetka.com.ua` (Cloudflare), with default settings
we got a `Just a moment...` interstitial on every attempt; after aligning the UA with
`--user-agent`, the same command returned the full catalogue (60 product tiles, 1.6 MB).
Nothing else changed. So this single inconsistency is enough to trigger a challenge that
would otherwise not fire.

Suggested fix: derive both the header and the JS-visible values from one source of truth,
and default that source to the actual host platform.


### Does headless Chrome behave the same?

No: headless Chrome renders or behaves correctly and obscura does not
